made_by: Coordinator #08, following D150 ruling 7 that the live lanes need no forecasting edge
authority: coordinator; market-lane measurement over witnessed prices. Uses no outcome and tests no hypothesis about player performance, so raises no partition question - the same footing M07, M17 and M27 operated on. Carries no executability claim.
question: D150 said the lanes that remain live need no forecasting edge, and named line shopping free, mechanical and currently unexploited. Free is a claim. What is it actually worth, and how close does this market really come to arbitrage?

ruling.1_LINE_SHOPPING_REMOVES_A_QUARTER_OF_THE: Measured over 179 snapshots and 2,591 PRE-GAME two-sided markets with a mean of 5.9 books quoting both sides: median overround **at one book 4.753%**, median overround **taking the best price on each side 3.477%**. **Line shopping removes 1.276 points, or 26.8% of the vig.** In breakeven terms it moves the required win rate on a two-way market from 52.38% to 51.74% - **0.64 points of win rate handed back, for free, mechanically, with no opinion about any game.** It is NOT an edge and cannot make a negative-expectation bet positive; it lowers the price of bets already being placed.
ruling.2_M28_HAD_A_BUG_THAT_WOULD_HAVE_STAKED_P: **THE BOARD SHIPPED YESTERDAY DID NOT FILTER IN-PLAY GAMES.** Measured: **24.56% of IN-PLAY two-sided markets show a negative cross-book overround, against 0.27% pre-game. 85.7% of all apparent arbitrage on this tape is in-play.** The mechanism was found by reading raw quotes: in Sparks @ Lynx captured 2026-08-07T03:00Z for a game that tipped at 01:05Z, fanduel had the Sparks at -7000 and betrivers at -10000 while **mybookieag still showed +125** - a pre-game price on a nearly finished game. **Quote age does not detect this**: mybookieag re-stamped last_update at 02:58 without moving the price, so the stale quote looks fresh. Since tier 1 is the only tier carrying a concrete stake, an unfiltered board would have handed out confident stakes on unfillable prices. **FIXED**: Quote.is_in_play, both the arbitrage and middle detectors now pre-game only, the excluded count surfaced in the board rather than dropped silently, and eight regression tests added (128/128).
ruling.3_THE_HONEST_PRE_GAME_ARBITRAGE_RATE_IS_: With in-play removed, **7 of 2,591 pre-game markets (0.2702%) show a negative best-price overround, the largest being 1.686%** and most under 0.5%. Every one involves mainstream books disagreeing modestly - draftkings, betrivers, fanduel, williamhill - which is what real, brief cross-book arbitrage looks like. **This is the honest context for M28 reporting zero on any given snapshot**: at roughly one market in 370, and on an hourly grid until today, finding none is the expected observation rather than a broken detector.
ruling.4_A_FALSE_HEADLINE_WAS_CAUGHT_BEFORE_IT_: The first pass produced **1.77% of markets showing arbitrage** - a striking number that would have been reported as a finding. It was wrong. Two successive filters failed to explain it: an outlier-ratio guard removed only 14 quotes of thousands, and a staleness test showed the suspect legs were FRESH (median 0.97 min old against 0.50 for all quotes). Only reading the raw JSON for a single game revealed that the games had already started. **Two plausible mechanisms were tested and rejected before the real one was found, and none of the three was reported until the raw data settled it.**

discipline: A 1.77% arbitrage rate is exactly the kind of headline this programme exists to distrust, and it was distrusted: three mechanisms were tested and the first two were wrong. The bug found is in the coordinator's own shipped node from the previous day, and it is recorded as a defect that would have cost money rather than as a refinement. The in-play exclusion is surfaced as a count in the board output rather than applied silently, per the no-silent-caps discipline.

question: M10_MIDDLES built the middle scanner and recorded in its own 'what could not be established' that it computed no probability model and reported no EV for any candidate. ruling.1_MOST_MIDDLES_THIS_BOARD_SURFACED_WERE_: **8 of the 9 middles on the live board are NEGATIVE EV.** At standard -110/-110 pricing a middle needs to hit **4.762%** of the time to break even, which requires a window of **1.81 points**. The board was surfacing 1.0- and 1.5-point windows, which hit an estimated 2.63% and 3.95% and are worth **-4.06 and -1.55 dollars per 200 staked**. The single positive one clears by **+1.05 on 200**. A tier labelled 'bounded risk' was quietly a tier of value-destroying bets, and the board said nothing either way because it had no probability to say it with.
ruling.2_HOW_THE_PROBABILITY_IS_DERIVED_AND_WHA: Dispersion of final totals measured on the **exploration partition only** (2021-2024, 888 games): sd 17.30, no market data involved. Dispersion of the posted line across games from the capture tape: sd 8.37, **using no outcome**, so no partition question arises. Variance decomposition gives residual sd **15.14**. Assumptions, named: the line is an unbiased conditional mean uncorrelated with its residual; the residual is approximately Gaussian on a discrete mildly-skewed variable; the window sits CENTRED on the line, so every figure is an UPPER bound because an off-centre window hits less; and sd_line rests on 48 games, which is the weakest input.
ruling.3_THE_CONCLUSION_SURVIVES_THE_ASSUMPTION: Using the UNCONDITIONAL sd (17.30) instead of the residual (15.14) LOWERS every hit rate, because a wider distribution puts less mass in a narrow window. **The favourable assumption is the one used, and even it calls 1.0- and 1.5-point middles negative.** The decomposition can be wrong in the direction that matters and the headline does not move. Both estimates are carried on every row.
ruling.4_WHAT_THE_BOARD_DOES_NOW: Every middle carries its expected value, its modelled hit rate against the breakeven rate, and the breakeven window at its own prices. Middles are **ranked by EV** rather than by window-per-unit-cost, which was the previous rank and is now visibly the wrong ordering. **Negative-EV middles are still SHOWN, labelled NEGATIVE EV, with the breakeven window named** - hiding them would be a silent cap, and a reader who sees a short list has learned nothing about what was filtered. The hit rate is labelled a MODEL, never a measurement, on every row.
ruling.5_WHAT_THIS_STILL_DOES_NOT_DO: It does not size anything - M24_STAKING remains gated behind M23 and M22, and the equal-stake figures illustrate payoff shape only. It does not model the push branch on whole-number edges. It does not model an off-centre window, which is why the numbers are upper bounds. And it does not measure realised middle-hit frequency, which would need paired historical lines and outcomes that this programme does not hold for the exploration partition - the totals in drive_masters are spreads and moneyline only (D147).

discipline: The measurement was built because a predecessor node wrote down what it had not done, and the honest reading of that note was that the board inheriting it was incomplete rather than finished. The fix shows the losing rows rather than filtering them away, and the robustness check was run against the assumption that most favours the conclusion rather than the one that flatters it.
preserved_disagreement: sd_line rests on 48 games of a single season's tape and is the weakest input in the chain. If the true line dispersion is materially larger, the residual shrinks, hit rates rise and the breakeven window narrows - possibly enough to make 1.5-point middles positive. A reader could reasonably hold that a 48-game estimate should not be load-bearing for a product rule. question: How much money can each measured opportunity class actually absorb? M22 was parked as unrunnable for want of live tape.

ruling.1_THE_NODE_WAS_NEVER_UNRUNNABLE_IT_WAS_B: M22 sat parked on the ground that it 'requires live multi-book capture tape that a clean checkout cannot supply'. **That premise was D138 in another costume**: the tape existed and had existed for weeks; the worktree could not see it. D146 fixed the access and the node ran the same day. **A second parked node was unparked by fixing a path, not by acquiring data.**
ruling.2_ARBITRAGE_IS_NOT_A_BUSINESS_AND_THE_AR: 0.270% of pre-game markets (D151) x ~9 markets/day = **one opportunity every 41 days**. Median observed size ~0.4%, largest 1.686%. Measured depth at best price (M21, real resting orders): **median $49.01**. **Profit per occurrence at median depth: $0.20 for a typical arb, $0.83 for the largest observed.** Upper bound: **single-digit dollars per season.** It is worth scanning only because the scanner already exists and costs nothing to run.
ruling.3_LINE_SHOPPING_IS_A_DISCOUNT_NOT_INCOME: Bounded by YOUR OWN TURNOVER rather than by the market - 1.276 vig points, 26.8% of the overround. $64/yr on $5,000 of turnover, $319 on $25,000, $1,276 on $100,000. **It does not generate money; it stops a fixed percentage of your own money leaking.** Bet nothing and it is worth nothing, which is exactly why it is the safest thing measured and also why it can never be a strategy by itself.
ruling.4_PROMOTIONS_ARE_THE_LARGEST_PER_UNIT_VA: $10.22 on a $25 free bet, $16.45 on a $50 bonus-back, $5.50 on a $25 boost - against $0.20 for a typical arbitrage. The per-offer bound is real; the number of offers is unknown, and this node declines to assume one.
ruling.5_THE_RANKING_INVERTS_THE_PROGRAMME_S_OW: By upper bound: **promotions, then line shopping, then arbitrage, then middles (negative), then model edge (zero).** **THE TWO CLASSES WORTH ANYTHING REQUIRE NO FORECASTING ABILITY WHATSOEVER.** The one this programme spent roughly 58 screens building toward is last, at zero. That is not an argument that the modelling was worthless - it produced the machinery and the discipline that made these measurements trustworthy - but it is a plain statement about where value was found.

discipline: The node's own acceptance criteria forbid a revenue projection, so every figure is framed as an upper bound with its assumptions beside it, and the largest class is reported with its frequency explicitly unmeasured rather than annualised on a guess. question: A mirrored-point bug was found in the promo valuation. Does the same assumption appear elsewhere, and did it affect anything already reported?

ruling.1_THE_SAME_BUG_WAS_IN_TWO_MORE_PLACES_AN: The promo fix exposed a CLASS of bug: pairing a two-sided market on the SIGNED point. Totals share one number (Over 181.5 / Under 181.5); **spreads carry opposite numbers (-8.5 / +8.5)**, so keying on the signed value puts each side in its own group, no group ever holds two outcomes, and every spread is silently discarded. An audit found it in **best_price_table** (98 spread quotes across 5 games producing 0 rows) and in **line_shopping.py**, which produced D151's headline.
ruling.2_D151_S_NUMBER_IS_CORRECTED_DOWNWARD: **Reported: line shopping removes 1.276 vig points, 26.8% of the overround, over 2,591 markets.** **Corrected: 1.157 points, 24.3%, over 4,460 markets.** Spread markets in the sample rise from **29 to 1,613** - the 29 that previously survived were pick-em lines where both sides genuinely share point 0. The direction is explicable rather than mysterious: spreads carry a higher best-price overround (3.600%) than moneylines (2.645%), so including them lowers the average benefit.
ruling.3_WHAT_SURVIVES_AND_WHAT_DOES_NOT: **The qualitative finding survives**: line shopping removes about a QUARTER of the vig, is free, mechanical and needs no opinion. **The specific figure does not**: 26.8% was measured on a sample missing 1,584 spread markets and should not be quoted again. ruling.4_THE_BOARD_NOW_SHOWS_SPREADS_WHICH_IT_N: The best-price table returns 6 spread rows where it returned none, and they carry real value - Atlanta -105 at DraftKings against a typical price, +4.00%, across 8 books; the vig on that market falls 4.73% -> 1.96% by shopping. **A whole market was invisible on the surface built to tell the user where to bet.**
ruling.5_HOW_IT_WAS_FOUND_AND_WHY_THAT_MATTERS: Not by a test, not by review. By building add_promo.py, pointing its --list at real data, and reading a column of 'consensus n/a (0 books)' next to every spread. The same is true of the in-play arbitrage bug (D151), which only appeared when raw quotes for one game were read by hand. **Both bugs produced silence rather than an error, and silence is invisible to a test suite that does not know what it should be seeing.** 174 assertions passed throughout, before and after, because none of them asserted that spreads should appear at all.

discipline: A bug found in one module was treated as a hypothesis about the codebase rather than an isolated defect, and the audit found it twice more - including under a number already reported to the user. The corrected figure is worse than the one originally published.
preserved_disagreement: A reader could argue 26.8% vs 24.3% is immaterial and the correction is noise. The coordinator disagrees on principle rather than magnitude: the original was computed on a sample that silently excluded a third of the market universe, and a number is not merely imprecise when its denominator was wrong - it was measuring something other than what it claimed.

authority: coordinator; no user gate touched. SHADOW mode unchanged, no stake emitted.
question: Spread middles were declared out of scope by the coverage audit because the dispersion of MARGINS had never been measured. Can the declaration be discharged into an implementation, and is the middle EV model correct?
ruling:
TWO CORRECTIONS, ONE PLANNED AND ONE NOT.

1. SPREAD MIDDLES ARE NOW IMPLEMENTED. The missing quantity was measured on the exploration partition: signed margin sd 13.73, spread-line sd 3.852 from tape using no outcome, giving a residual of 13.18 around the posted spread. Margins are TIGHTER than totals (residual 15.10), so a spread middle breaks even at a NARROWER window - 1.56 points against 1.80 - which makes spread middles slightly easier to profit from than the totals middles this board already carried. The declared gap is discharged; the audit entry is replaced by an implementation and the test that guarded the excuse now guards the code.

2. THE PUSH BRANCH WAS MISPRICED ON BOTH SURFACES, AND WAS ALMOST SHIPPED AS A CAVEAT SAYING SO DIDN'T MATTER. The window model is open at both ends, so it scored 'the game landed exactly on a whole-number line' as a MISS. It is not a miss: that leg is REFUNDED while the other wins, so the outcome is better than modelled by one full stake. The coordinator first wrote a caveat asserting the effect was 'not by enough to change the sign at these prices' - an unmeasured claim - then measured it. WNBA margins pile up on the low key numbers: P(margin exactly 3) is 5.4%, worth +5.36 on 200 staked, which moved a 2.5/3 spread middle from -6.11 to -0.75. That is an order of magnitude larger than 'negligible'. It is now PRICED on both spread and totals middles rather than disclaimed, with the uncorrected figure retained on every row so the correction is auditable. Today one middle on the live board is positive expectation where none was.
discipline:
The push correction is signed: it can only ever help the holder, so where the measured support runs out the correction is DROPPED rather than extrapolated - the model understates rather than oversells. Sizing remains gated (M24 <- M23 <- M22); no middle emits a stake. Exploration partition only; 2025/2026 were not read, joined, plotted or described. The line-dispersion term still comes from holdout-era tape, admissible because it uses no outcome (D147: no exploration-era market lines exist).
SEPARATELY, A SOURCE DEFECT WAS FOUND AND FIXED. The team-level gamelogs give only 730 exploration games because 2024 REGULAR SEASON is absent from refresh_2026 - only its playoffs are present. An earlier pass of this measurement reported 888 on a different partial set. Aggregating player-level logs to team recovers the full 970. Every figure here is on 970. The same complete set independently reproduces SD_TOTAL_EXPLORATION at 17.396 against the 17.30 carried from M10, which corroborates that constant.
preserved_disagreement: A reader could argue the push table is over-fitted: per-value rates rest on tens of games and are three-point smoothed, and the smoothing choice is a judgement. The coordinator accepts the estimate is noisy in its third digit and denies this weakens the ruling, because the decision-relevant fact is that the branch exists and is worth several percent of a stake, not its precise value. A reader could also argue that implementing a surface which today produces only negative-expectation rows is wasted work; the coordinator disagrees - the surface reports a measured NO, which is a different and more useful state than silence, and it will fire when a 2-point window appears.

authority: coordinator. No user gate touched, no stake emitted, SHADOW unchanged. Uses MARKET PRICES ONLY - no game outcome is read, so the confirmation holdout is untouched (same admissibility as D147).
question: The board flags books whose prices disagree with their peers and calls them 'stale by design' because nobody had measured what the disagreement is worth. When a book disagrees, who moves - and does the movement beat the vig?
ruling:
WHO MOVES: THE OUTLIER, ESSENTIALLY ENTIRELY. A dislocation of >=1.5pp of de-vigged probability shrinks 0.491pp [0.426,0.574] over an hourly horizon, of which 0.479pp is the outlier moving and 0.131pp [-0.047,0.235] is consensus moving - the latter is not distinguishable from zero. P4 IS REFUTED: no book leads. There is a consensus, and there are books that wander from it and come back. Which makes peer consensus the right anchor and settles what the dispersion flags are pointing at.

WHETHER IT PAYS: THE THRESHOLD IS ABOUT 2 POINTS, AND THE PRIZE IS SMALL. Charging the full vig of the book actually bet and crediting us with no forecasting skill: betting blind loses 4.43% a stake; always taking the best of eleven books still loses 2.05%; a book generous by >=1.5pp loses 0.63%; >=2.0pp breaks even (CI spans zero); >=3.0pp earns +1.44%. Collapsed to distinct opportunities, >=3pp arrives 0.13-0.46 times per game, so a ~200-game season offers roughly 26-92 qualifying bets at +1% to +3%. At >=2.0pp the MEDIAN opportunity is 0.000%/-0.266% - that bucket is mean-positive on a tail and is not reliably positive bet by bet, so 3pp is the honest line.

THE REPLICATION IS WHAT MAKES THIS CREDIBLE. The 2025-26 hist family (411 games) was reserved by the prereg and not consulted until the live headline was written down. The fraction of quotes beating peer consensus agrees to two decimals across independent samples (1.18% and 1.18%), and the >=1.5pp bucket agrees to a hundredth of a percent (-0.633% and -0.622%).

CONSEQUENCE FOR THE PRODUCT: the board's dispersion flags acquire a defensible cut. Under 2pp is not an opportunity and must not be presented as one; 3pp is where acting is justified. None of this involves a scoring model, so none of it is exposed to S42 or to D141/D150's finding that our model trails the market. It also BOUNDS the prize, and the bound is small - the same verdict as D153 on arbitrage, one rung less severe.
discipline:
THE PREREGISTERED PRIMARY TEST IS NOT EVALUATED, AND IS NOT QUIETLY REPLACED. The frozen statistic was a median; it returned 0.000 everywhere because 65.8% of dislocated books do not move at all over the horizon and 32.9% of observations have neither side moving. A median over a point mass that large reports the point mass. P1, P2 and P3 are unevaluated; s01 and its degenerate FINDINGS.json are kept exactly as frozen; everything else in the node is labelled POST-HOC in the files themselves and may not be quoted as confirmed. Five defects are recorded in DEFECTS.md rather than repaired: (1) the degenerate median; (2) last_update cannot detect staleness because the feed re-stamps it on every poll - 99.6% of consecutive captures look fresh while 82.6% of prices are identical, so the gate was reimplemented on price identity and the substitution disclosed; (3) discrete odds mean reversion cannot be separated from regression to the mean, so no claim is made about which books are informed; (4) 48 live games spanning a six-day capture blackout; (5) the horizon is defined on CONSECUTIVE captures, which ties it to the polling rate - now that capture runs every five minutes no pair qualifies, so extending the tape pin added exactly zero observations and nothing here describes sub-hour dynamics.
A SIXTH FAULT WAS FOUND IN THIS NODE'S OWN LOADER AND FIXED: it tested isinstance(blob, list) and silently dropped all 292 hist files, which are wrapped as {timestamp, data:[...]}. The replication reported 'no observations' rather than failing. That is the same silent-absence class as D138, D151 and D155 - the fourth occurrence. The loader now COLLECTS AND REPORTS every file it cannot parse, and an empty result is fatal rather than a finding.
preserved_disagreement: A reader could argue the whole node is circular: it measures edge against peer consensus, so it can only ever find that outliers are wrong, and if the entire market is mispriced it would score the one correct book as the mistake. The coordinator accepts this completely and denies it damages the ruling, because the claim made is deliberately narrow - it is a claim about closing-line value against the market's own settling point, not about truth, and it is stated that way in the report. A reader could also argue that 26-92 bets a season at 1-3% is not worth building for. The coordinator does not disagree about the magnitude and notes it is the first positive-expectation route this programme has measured that requires no forecasting model at all.
evidence: PREREG.md sha256 895d004fceaf3c3f64bc0d2f04e581520c284925d2af089672b8e5f2d0371f87, frozen before any statistic. Tape pinned at 2026-08-19T23:05:00Z and recorded in every FINDINGS file. live: 54,524 pre-game quotes over 48 games; hist: 66,967 over 411 games; 11 books. s01 FINDINGS.json (degenerate, kept), s02 FINDINGS_s02.json, s03 FINDINGS_s03.json, REPORT.md, DEFECTS.md. CONSEQUENCE: PREREG.md still reads 'M29 PRICE LEADERSHIP' in a node called M30, and that discrepancy stays. A frozen document keeps its original text, cosmetic defects included. verify.py asserts BOTH that the hash matches and that the old title is still present, so a future tidy-up of that line fails the node instead of passing quietly.

The near-miss is the reason it exists: the hash check would have caught this on the next run, so it now runs on every run rather than on request.

authority: coordinator; amends validate_graph.py check 5. Records openly that the change was prompted by the coordinator's own node failing the rule.
question: validate_graph.py requires every node of type 'experiment' to have an ancestor whose id contains PREREG or FREEZE_TASK_CARDS. M30 carries a hash-frozen preregistration inside itself and has no such ancestor. Does the rule bend, or does the node?
ruling:
THE RULE IS AMENDED, AND MADE STRICTER IN THE PROCESS. The requirement that matters is a FROZEN PREREGISTRATION; what the rule actually tested was a NAMING CONVENTION on an ancestor node. Those coincide in the player program, where a preregistration node freezes task cards and experiments sit downstream, but they are not the same thing. A single-node measurement that carries its own prereg satisfies the purpose directly.

Check 5 now passes an experiment if EITHER (a) an ancestor is named as a preregistration node, as before, OR (b) the node pins its own PREREG file in input_hashes - and branch (b) is verified far more strictly than (a) ever was: the file must exist on disk AND still hash to the pinned value. Form (a) never confirmed that any preregistration had actually been frozen, only that a node with the right name was upstream. So the graph is now harder to cheat than it was before this amendment, not easier.

The new branch was tested by tampering: appending one byte to M30's PREREG.md makes validate_graph.py exit 1 naming the file, the pinned hash and the actual hash, and instructing that the bytes be restored rather than the pin updated. Restoring returns it to exit 0. A relaxed gate that cannot be shown to bite is not a gate.
discipline: This amendment was written by the same party whose node failed the rule, which is exactly the situation in which a rule tends to get quietly loosened. Three things guard against that here: the amendment ADDS a verification that did not previously exist anywhere; the failure mode it introduces was demonstrated before the change was committed; and the reasoning is recorded in the validator source at the point of the check, so a future reader meets the justification and not just the code. The alternative considered and rejected was mislabelling M30 as 'audit' or 'implementation' to dodge the rule, which would have hidden a real experiment from every experiment-specific check in the graph.
preserved_disagreement: A reader could argue the correct move was to create a separate M30A_PREREGISTRATION node and keep the rule untouched, since the existing structure already expresses this and inventing a second mechanism adds a way for the graph to be inconsistent with itself. The coordinator accepts this is defensible and chose otherwise because a preregistration node that exists only to satisfy a validator, freezing a file that lives in the node it would point at, is ceremony rather than control - and because the alternative left the weaker of the two checks in place as the only one.
evidence: scripts/validate_graph.py check 5, amended with both branches and the reasoning in-source. Tamper test: one byte appended to PREREG.md -> exit 1 naming 895d004fceaf3c3f vs 0d22c5eb9b19266e; restored -> exit 0. Graph now validates at 107 nodes with 0 errors and 1 pre-existing unrelated warning (O16). M30 verify.py 25/25.

authority: coordinator. No user gate touched. Market prices only; no game outcome read.
question: M30 measured that a 3pp cross-book dislocation is worth +1.4%, but not how long one stays on the screen. The board refreshes every ten minutes. Is that fast enough to ever catch one - and how is that measured without the measurement being shaped by when it is taken?
ruling:
THE QUESTION IS FROZEN NOW; THE ANSWER WAITS FOR THE TAPE. The five-minute capture began 2026-08-19 and holds 5 games, 38 episodes and 3 strong episodes against a preregistered gate of 30 / 150 / 40. Three strong episodes cannot support a survival curve and a cluster bootstrap over five games is a decoration, not an interval. So nothing is computed.

PREREGISTERING BEFORE THE DATA EXISTS IS THE POINT, not an accident of timing. The estimator (Kaplan-Meier), the censoring rule, the strong/weak split, the horizon definition and the four predictions are all fixed while the answer is still unknowable, so none of them can be chosen to suit it.

THE SAMPLE GATE IS ENFORCED IN CODE, NOT BY INTENTION. s01_persistence.py refuses to compute the primary while the gate is closed, and verify.py fails if the thresholds are edited. This defends against one specific failure that leaves no trace: recomputing the curve every day and publishing on whichever day it looks best is choosing the answer while appearing to measure it. A fixed threshold on SAMPLE SIZE, set before any data existed, removes the opportunity rather than relying on a successor's restraint. Note that a coordinator with a standing instruction to keep producing findings is exactly the actor most exposed to that temptation.

WHAT THE ANSWER WILL DECIDE. If a 3pp dislocation typically survives half an hour, the board catches it and the M30 edge is reachable. If it typically survives five minutes, the board is structurally incapable of ever showing one in time and no amount of ranking or presentation repairs that - the finding would be about our polling rate, not about the market, and the remedy would be M27_PER_BOOK_POLLING rather than anything in M28.
discipline: M30's DEFECT 5 is fixed at the source rather than inherited: the horizon here is defined in CLOCK TIME, never in 'consecutive captures', so the measurement does not change meaning when the polling rate changes - which is precisely what silently emptied M30 of every five-minute observation. Right-censoring is specified in the preregistration rather than left to analysis-time judgement, because dropping still-open episodes shortens every lifetime and biases the result toward the flattering 'act fast' conclusion. Episodes straddling a capture gap wider than twelve minutes are DISCARDED AND COUNTED (10 so far), since an episode spanning a blackout has an unknown lifetime that must not be fabricated - capture coverage is 61% and the laptop sleeps (D154). The five-minute grid is a resolution floor and is recorded as an UPWARD bias on every lifetime the node can ever report, meaning the actionability prediction is measured optimistically.
preserved_disagreement: A reader could argue this is over-engineering: 38 episodes already hint at an answer, the hint could be published with a caveat, and a hard-coded refusal is theatre. The coordinator disagrees on the specific ground that this programme has already published and later corrected numbers computed on samples that turned out to be wrong (D155, and D157's own 888-versus-970 game count), and that a caveat has never yet stopped a number from being quoted without it. A reader could also argue the gate thresholds are arbitrary. They are judgement, not derivation - but they were set before any result was visible, which is the property that matters.

Graph validates at 108 nodes, 0 errors. Gate expected to open around 2026-08-27 at the earliest.

authority: coordinator, on direct user instruction to re-run the matchup family on rate. Exploration partition 2021-2024 only; 2025/2026 never read. No wager-shaped claim; S42 stands.
question: Every matchup screen measured its channel against POINTS, which is minutes x rate, and minutes carry about half the variance. Were the nulls real, or were they diluted by the wrong denominator?
ruling:
THE NULLS WERE REAL. Dilution exists and is small: for the one channel resolvable on both responses the rate/points ratio is 1.21, and the coordinator had preregistered >1.5 and was wrong. Nothing that previously read null came alive.

ONE CHANNEL SURVIVES, AND IT IS NOT NEW. Opponent defensive strength, best expressed as an interaction with the player's own prior usage: dR2 +0.003737 on rate, p_fwe 0.0005 against 2000 opponent-team-season permutations. That is D093's structural fact and E1_I0023's SPLIT verdict, now cleared against a proper family-wise correction with a negative control and a measured detection floor.

THE SHOT-ZONE IDEA IS CLOSED IN ITS FORECASTABLE FORM. Built pregame-observably from the player's PRIOR zone shares dotted with the opponent's prior zone leakiness, it returns dR2 -0.000204, below the floor, UNRESOLVED. The earlier screen's strong zone result conditioned on the player's REALISED in-game attempts, which is not knowable pre-tip. The coordinator had named this the most promising candidate; it is the weakest.

MEASURING ON RATE IS STILL THE RIGHT CHOICE, for a smaller reason than the one given: the matchup increment is 35% larger on rate, and routing through rate x minutes rather than modelling points directly improves MAE 0.458% all in, of which the matchup stack is 0.0131 points. For scale, plain average -> tuned EWMA was worth 2.0%, so the entire matchup family measured the better way is about a quarter of that.

THE NEGATIVE CONTROL WORKED. Opponent pace, preregistered as a control because pace moves volume rather than efficiency, returned dR2 -0.004182 with p_fwe 1.0000. The pipeline is not leaking, which is what licenses reading the rest.

WHERE THE ROOM ACTUALLY IS: the base reaches R2 0.156 on points-per-minute against 0.478 on points. Most of what is predictable about a player's scoring is HOW LONG THEY PLAY, not how well. The matchup family is not where the remaining accuracy lives.
discipline:
Five defects recorded in DEFECTS.md rather than repaired. Two are the coordinator's own.
(1) THE MOTIVATING CLAIM FAILED ITS OWN PREREGISTERED TEST. The coordinator told the user matchup effects were diluted 2.4x, citing D099's 0.0113 ppm vs 0.0046 points. Those came from a different row set and a different base. Recomputed on one common frame the ratio is 1.21. This is the SAME error E1_I0027 recorded as the programme's larger defect - ordering quantities that are not commensurable - committed again, by the coordinator, three messages after summarising that very finding.
(2) THE PREREGISTERED DESIGN OVER-COUNTS CHANNELS. Each channel was an increment over a common base, but C3a is BUILT from C1, so the design cannot separate an interaction from the main effect inside it. C3c cleared the family-wise correction at p_fwe 0.0490 and then contributed -0.000169 once C1 and C3a were present. Without the unplanned nested test this screen would have published THREE surviving channels. There is one.
(3) The injection calibration over-recovers by 2.3x to 6.9x, so the detection floor is a valid UPPER BOUND (<= 0.001) and not the calibrated quantity the prereg described.
C2 and C3b are reported UNRESOLVED, not null - they sit below the floor, and 'we could not see it' is not 'it is not there'. That conflation is precisely what the old archetype screen's 200-permutation design forced, and this screen used 2000 draws against a rank-1 BH threshold of 0.0167 specifically so it could not recur.
preserved_disagreement: A reader could argue the screen buries its own positive result: a channel clearing p_fwe 0.0005 with a clean negative control is a genuine confirmation, and leading with the failed dilution prediction understates it. The coordinator accepts the confirmation is real and leads with the failure anyway, because the screen was commissioned on the strength of the dilution argument and a reader who is not told it failed cannot price the rest. A reader could also argue C2's construction was too crude to close the zone idea on - a single dot product rather than zone-level rate forecasts - and the coordinator agrees, which is why DEFECT 5 states the closure applies to this construction only.
evidence: PREREG.md sha256 d53637d0fbe9971e2051316003af05cbc9dff64c58f318a8ff9d21194e4e1b7c, frozen after frame shape and before any effect. 14,259 complete rows, 242 players, 861 games, 48 opponent-team-seasons, 11,279 scored. 2000 permutations of opponent-team-season within season; cluster and max-t both reported. FINDINGS.json, REPORT.md, DEFECTS.md. Predictions: P1 PASS, P2 FAIL, P3 PASS (gutted post-hoc), P4 PASS, P5 PASS.

authority: coordinator, on direct user instruction to focus on minutes. Exploration 2021-2024 only. No wager-shaped claim; S42 stands.
question: The mean of minutes is heavily mined - E1_I0053 returned seven of eight candidates null and found the team-budget gain was an overtime oracle worth zero pre-game. The shipped uncertainty is a per-season scalar and every alternative tried has been point +/- k*sd. Minutes are bounded, flat-topped (kurtosis -1.03) and carry a spike at zero. Does modelling the DISTRIBUTION rather than the scale unlock anything?
ruling:
THE DISTRIBUTION WORK IS REAL AND SMALL. Holding the point forecast identical across every arm, conditional empirical residual quantiles improve PIT calibration THREEFOLD (chi2 90.1 -> 30.7) but move CRPS +0.83%, against the >3% preregistered. Per-row SCALE modelling is outright NEGATIVE (-0.30%), which is the second time it has failed - E1_I0056 increment already straddled zero. Stop rescaling minutes uncertainty; it does not work.

THE BRANCH NOBODY MODELS IS WORTH MORE THAN EVERY REFINEMENT COMBINED. Multiplying the played-branch distribution by P(play) with an explicit point mass at zero improves the Brier score on 'more than 15 minutes' by 11.5%, and improves at all five thresholds (+11.5/+7.7/+4.8/+2.5/+0.8%). The gradient is exactly right: a player who does not dress cannot clear a low line, and by t>35 the question is rotation size rather than availability. Read against that, ALL the distributional shape work is worth nothing for a threshold question - the shape arm is a hair WORSE than the constant-sd Gaussian at three of five thresholds.

AND THE 11.5% IS A FLOOR. It was obtained with a deliberately crude availability estimate, an EWMA of the player prior appearance rate, which E0_I0019 measured at Brier 0.122 / AUC 0.841. The programme ALREADY HOLDS a far better one - the shipped p_active at 0.092 / 0.902 - and it is not wired into any minutes forecast.

SO THE USER PREMISE IS HALF RIGHT AND THE HALF THAT IS WRONG MATTERS. Minutes are not badly predicted - the ladder puts them at R2 0.668 against points at 0.523, so minutes are already the BETTER-predicted quantity. The room was never in predicting them more precisely. It is in the branch where there are none.
discipline:
SIX DEFECTS RECORDED, and the first is a labelling error that invalidates a prediction rather than a result. The arm named A0_SHIPPED_STYLE is NOT the shipped model: its constant is fitted on strictly earlier residuals of this screen own point forecast, so it is a CORRECTLY calibrated constant-sd Gaussian covering 0.8056 at nominal 0.80. E1_I0056 measured 0.685 on the actual emitted bytes of a badly chosen constant. P1 failed because I wrote the prediction as though the two objects were the same. NOTHING HERE REFUTES E1_I0056 AND THE SHIPPED CONSTANT IS STILL WRONG AND STILL UNREPAIRED. The arm keeps its frozen name and the correction is recorded instead.
FOUR OF SIX PREDICTIONS FAILED (P1, P3, P4, P5). The thesis P2 survives in DIRECTION only: the scale gain is negative, so the preregistered 'at least twice' ratio has a negative denominator and is not a quantity. P4 predicted signature was backwards - I predicted excess PIT mass in the outer bins and the misfit is in the INTERIOR, which is what a flat-topped response does to a bell-shaped forecast and is what the kurtosis of -1.03 printed before freezing should have told me.
The screen has NOT tested what it recommends: A4 uses the weaker availability instrument, so the recommendation to wire in p_active needs its own preregistered screen.
preserved_disagreement: A reader could argue the availability finding is trivially obvious - of course a model that knows a player might not play beats one that assumes they will - and that dressing it as a finding overstates it. The coordinator agrees it is obvious in hindsight and notes it has nonetheless never been done: minutes_baselines defines its prediction universe as played rows only, and E1_I0053 and E1_I0056 both work exclusively on played strata. The obvious thing was measured for the first time here, and it is larger than everything the non-obvious work produced. A reader could also argue the shape work should be discarded at +0.83%; the coordinator would keep it for the threefold calibration gain, which costs nothing and matters for any interval this programme ever publishes.
evidence: PREREG.md sha256 e44c46a5f2b83da6f3834ddcb7b7816b8abe0419bad74c4d74c2478c0f99244a, frozen after the response shape statistics and before any score. 12,281 scored played rows over 450 player-seasons; 14,342 dressed rows. Identical point forecast in every arm. CRPS on a common 0.25-minute grid; cluster bootstrap by player-season, 2000 draws. Conditional-bin fallback rate 0.0008. FINDINGS.json, REPORT.md, DEFECTS.md. P1 FAIL, P2 PASS (direction only), P3 FAIL, P4 FAIL, P5 FAIL, P6 PASS.

authority: coordinator, on direct user instruction to wire in the good availability model and measure it. Exploration 2022-2024 only. No wager-shaped claim; S42 stands.
question: E1_I0061 found that adding ANY availability branch to a minutes forecast beats having none, using a deliberately crude instrument, and then recommended wiring in the shipped p_active WITHOUT TESTING IT. Does the good instrument deliver, and how much of the value is in having a branch versus having a good one?
ruling:
CONFIRMED, AND LARGER THAN THE FLOOR E1_I0061 LEFT. With the minutes point forecast and the played-branch distribution held identical across every arm, so the availability term is the only thing varying: Brier on P(minutes > 15) improves 17.8% against no branch, versus the 11.3% the crude instrument delivered on the same rows. CRPS over the dressed distribution goes 4.33012 -> 3.75864 -> 3.54549, an 18.1% improvement end to end with non-overlapping intervals between no-branch and good.

ALL FIVE PREDICTIONS PASSED, INCLUDING THE SCEPTICAL ONE. P2 held: having a branch at all is worth more (+0.01442 [+0.00852, +0.02143]) than upgrading it (+0.00822 [+0.00591, +0.01067]) - but the upgrade adds 57% on top and its interval is tighter and further from zero. The practical ordering is that not modelling availability is the large error and using a bad availability model is a second error about half as large again.

THE BETTER MODEL IS THE WORSE-CALIBRATED ONE, AND THAT IS FINE. p_active under-predicts availability by 4.3 points on this row set (mean 0.8141 against an actual 0.8575) and is nearly three times worse on calibration deviation than the crude prior-rate, yet wins decisively on Brier (0.07902 vs 0.08588) and AUC (0.8977 vs 0.8599). It is the better RANKER and the worse CALIBRATOR, and the mixture needs ranking.

DO NOT RECALIBRATE IT FIRST. Walk-forward logistic recalibration does exactly what it should to the instrument - Brier 0.07884 -> 0.07770, mean prediction 0.8114 -> 0.8582 against an actual 0.8540 - AND MAKES THE MINUTES FORECAST WORSE: t>15 Brier 0.10438 -> 0.10515, CRPS 3.52561 -> 3.53438. The headroom the miscalibration appeared to leave is not there. That step is closed cheaply rather than being carried as an open lead.

THE GRADIENT REPRODUCES EXACTLY, which is the strongest internal evidence the mechanism is real rather than a fitting artefact: +17.8/+12.5/+7.8/+4.1/+1.2% across thresholds 15 to 35. Availability dominates at low lines, where failing to dress is the main way to miss, and fades to almost nothing by t>35 where the question becomes rotation size.
discipline:
SIX DEFECTS RECORDED. Two deserve emphasis.
ALL FIVE PREDICTIONS PASSING IS ITSELF A REASON FOR SUSPICION, and is recorded as DEFECT 2. Three of the five were close to guaranteed before running: P5 restates E0_I0019's measurement, P4 restates E1_I0061's measured gradient, and P1 is P5 pushed one step downstream. Only P2 carried genuine risk and only its failure would have changed a decision. The screen is a confirmation with one live question in it, not five independent successes, and should be read that way.
THE PROVENANCE IS INHERITED, NOT ESTABLISHED HERE (DEFECT 1). v15 p_active is consumed as an out-of-fold production artifact; its point-in-time discipline is E0_I0019's finding, reached after four leak-probe attempts of which three were withdrawn as confounded. This screen ran no probe of its own and has no independent standing if that verdict falls.
The post-hoc recalibration result is UNEXPLAINED (DEFECT 3). The report offers a mechanism - the played branch is fitted on players who played and so runs high for marginal players, which p_active's downward bias offsets - and that mechanism is a story attached to a number, not a tested claim. A compensating pair of biases is a fragile thing to ship and anyone acting on this should find out why first.
The played branch was RE-IMPLEMENTED rather than imported (DEFECT 6) because E1_I0061 wrote scores and not per-row CDFs. A difference there moves every arm identically and so cannot manufacture a between-arm result, which is why it was accepted, but absolute CRPS values here are not guaranteed to reproduce that screen's.
preserved_disagreement: A reader could argue this screen tells us nothing we did not already know - that a model with AUC 0.90 beats one with AUC 0.86 downstream is close to arithmetic, and dressing it as a finding inflates it. The coordinator largely agrees and has recorded exactly that as DEFECT 2. Two things survive the objection: the SIZE was not predictable from the instrument metrics alone, and the recalibration result is genuinely counterintuitive and would have been a plausible and wasted next step. A reader could also argue that shipping a deliberately miscalibrated probability into a production mixture is unacceptable regardless of measured performance; the coordinator has sympathy for this and notes DEFECT 3 leaves the question open rather than resolved.

Identical point forecast and played branch in every arm. Cluster bootstrap by player-season, 2000 draws, seed 20260820. FINDINGS.json, REPORT.md, DEFECTS.md. P1-P5 all PASS.

question: D092 recommended the cold-start rule, D137 authorised it on condition it reproduce its validated numbers, and D139 found the two cannot both hold: the headline 4.02 came from a variant INCLUDING listed position while D092 ruling 2 says to drop it. Which is the authorised object?
ruling:
THE SPECIFIED RULE, NOT THE VALIDATED NUMBER. The module implements the cold-start blend WITHOUT listed position, yielding tier MAE 4.032479 on points rather than the 4.024334 that D092 published as 4.02.

THE INCONSISTENCY IS NOW CONFIRMED AT THE LINE OF CODE, not merely asserted. s03_placeholders.py:193 builds P5c_additive as league + pos_dev + draft_dev + depth_dev, and the identity P5c_additive == P2_position + P3_draft_bin + P4_teamrole - 2*league holds to 7.105e-15 on the artifact. The recommended rule as computed did include position.

THREE REASONS FOR TAKING THE RULE OVER THE NUMBER. (1) D092 ruling 2 is the RULE; 4.02 is a number a superseded variant happened to produce. (2) Listed position is MEASURED NULL (p 0.783, permutation null 0.1996); carrying a null feature in order to land on a headline is backwards, and this programme's own habit note names restating-to-fit as its modal failure. (3) The gap is 0.008145 points of tier MAE, 0.20%, and +3.492% pooled skill against +3.507%. Immaterial to performance. The principle is not immaterial, which is why the alternative is kept reachable rather than deleted: structural_prior(include_listed_position=True) reproduces 4.024334 exactly, so reversing this ruling is a one-argument change and the user can do it.

EVERY VALIDATED NUMBER REPRODUCES. On the E1_I0020 artifact, 13,879 rows and 1,061 in tier: champion tier MAE 6.063956 points / 9.748011 minutes; own-running-mean-only 4.252020; authorised rule 4.032479 / 5.448707; position-inclusive 4.024334 / 5.437188. Pooled points skill against the D076 reference: champion -0.222%, running mean alone +3.090%, authorised rule +3.492%, position-inclusive +3.507%. D092's -0.22 / +3.09 / +3.51 all reproduce.

AND THE DEFECT IS CONFIRMED ON THE ARTIFACT: the champion's forecast standard deviation across those 1,061 rows is 0.012982 while the actual outcome spread is 7.22. The flatness is the forecast's, not the world's.

WORTH SAYING PLAINLY: FOUR FIFTHS OF THE REPAIR IS THE RUNNING MEAN. Splicing in the player's own games so far, with no priors and no draft data, moves pooled skill from -0.222% to +3.090%. The whole structural apparatus - depth-chart rank and draft slot - adds +0.402% on top. That is real and it is the last fifth. D092 said this in its own qualification 1 and it should not be lost when the rule is described.
discipline:
THE MODULE IS AVAILABLE, NOT BOUND. cbs_player_coldstart_v16.py plus its test suite are two NEW files; no existing file is touched. It is not wired into the live arm, so THE PRODUCTION DEFECT REMAINS LIVE. Binding requires revising a byte-locked arm-registry record and should follow a registered generation run - exactly the standard D139 held the dispersion repair to, and it is held to it here rather than waived because the user said 'fix it'.
28/28 own tests. The suite asserts BOTH variants to 5e-6 and asserts the 0.008145 gap explicitly, so the inconsistency lives in test output rather than only in a decision record; if that number ever moves, D139's finding has changed and the ledger must say so. A COORDINATOR ERROR WAS CAUGHT BY ITS OWN TEST: two minutes anchors were written to six decimals from a four-decimal printout - fabricated precision. The test failed, the true values were measured (9.748011, 5.448707, 5.437188) and the anchors corrected. Recorded because quoting more precision than was measured is the same class of error as quoting a number from an incommensurable setting, which this coordinator did in D161.
A PRE-EXISTING DEFECT WAS FOUND AND IS NOT REPAIRED HERE: tests/test_cbs_v15.py now scores 29/32 while the committed experiments/player_program/V15_MODULE_TEST_RECEIPT.json claims 32/32 and all_passed true. The coordinator accepts this is a fair reading of D137's literal text and acted otherwise for a stated reason - that D137's condition was plainly a guard against a change that does not work, not a demand for bit-exactness on a number computed from a variant its own ruling had already discarded - and has left the alternative one argument away precisely so that a user who disagrees can override it without re-deriving anything. authority: coordinator, on direct user instruction to bind the cold-start splice live. The code is built and tested. THE REGISTRY WAS NOT FLIPPED - see ruling 2 and 3, which are findings made while attempting it, not a refusal of the instruction.
question: Bind the cold-start splice into the live arm. What actually happened?
ruling:
1. THE FORK IS BUILT AND TESTED AND THE DEFECT IS GONE ON THE INTENDED ROWS. cbs_player_runner/17 is /16 forked at exactly one line, generated at import from inspect.getsource with the substitution asserted to match once: 'test, tgt, raw.where(lvl == 0, fb_mean)' becomes 'test, tgt, _cs.fold_point(raw, lvl, fb_mean)'. Four changed lines - the def rename and the seam. 33/33 tests. On /14's own fixture, NON-FALLBACK ROWS ARE BIT-IDENTICAL to /16, levels 1/3/4 are unchanged, and short-history forecasts stop being a constant: emitted sd goes from 0.0000 to 6.0347 on minutes, 2.7237 on points, 2.5531 on attempts. /16's dispersion repair is inherited and asserted still present.

THE MEASURED FACT THAT SHAPED THE DESIGN: the runner was throwing away information it already had. Of 1,061 cold-start rows, 990 carry at least one prior appearance, and on those rows the player's own centre is FINITE BY CONSTRUCTION - player_fallback_level assigns level 2 only when n_prior >= 1 and the centre is finite. The model computes the player's own history and then declines to use it on precisely the rows where it is the only information there is.

2. WHAT IS BINDABLE IS NOT THE AUTHORISED RULE, AND MUST NOT BE CALLED IT. D092's rule shrinks the own-mean toward a structural prior built from depth-chart rank and DRAFT SLOT. Draft slot is not reachable: the runner's registered feature sources are src_asof_gamelog, src_asof_roster and src_asof_schedule, and bios is not among them. Adding it is a contract change with provenance and registration consequences, not a seam. Substituting the pooled mean for the structural prior was measured and is WORSE than not blending at all - tier MAE 4.7611 against 4.2594 - because the pooled mean IS the constant the repair exists to escape. Shrinkage helps only toward something informative. So /17 does the reachable part: points tier MAE 4.2594 and pooled skill +3.077% against the authorised rule's 4.0325 and +3.492%; minutes 5.4947 / +9.728% against 5.4487 / +9.795%. From a champion baseline of -0.222% that is 89% of the available gain on points and 99% on minutes, for one line and no new input.

3. THE LIVE BINDING IS HELD, ON A BLOCKER FOUND WHILE ATTEMPTING IT. The live arm is cbs_v15_player_oof_v5, whose runner is cbs_player_runner/15. ITS OWN FORK-INTEGRITY TEST IS RED: tests/test_cbs_v15.py scores 29/32, failing 'exactly two changed lines' (4 found) and 'every estimator name resolves to v14's own object' (0 objects resolved, 14 names listed as differing). The committed V15_MODULE_TEST_RECEIPT.json claims 32/32 and all_passed true. The guarantee that the live arm is v14-plus-one-seam is therefore UNVERIFIED, and its receipt asserts the opposite. Binding a new runner into an arm whose fork integrity cannot currently be demonstrated would be building on an unverified base, and D139's standard - that binding follows a registered generation run - cannot be met honestly while the arm's own generation guarantee is red. This is reported rather than worked around.
discipline:
THE INSTRUCTION WAS TO BIND AND THE REGISTRY WAS NOT FLIPPED. That is a coordinator decision and is recorded as one so the user can overrule it immediately. The reasoning: binding is not a toggle - require_registered_identity asserts config_hash against a byte-locked REGISTERED_CONFIG_HASH, so changing what an arm emits requires a new registration and a generation run - and both blockers above were discovered during the attempt, not known beforehand. Blocker 3 in particular is the kind of thing this programme exists to catch, and shipping through it to satisfy an instruction would invert that.
WHAT WOULD MAKE THIS BINDABLE, in order: (a) resolve test_cbs_v15's fork integrity and regenerate its receipt, since a committed false green is the more serious of the two problems and is independent of cold start; (b) decide whether to bind /17 as the reachable 89%, or to add bios as a registered feature source and bind the full authorised rule; (c) register and run the generation.
The fork declares is_the_full_authorised_rule False in its own source_diff receipt, carries the 4.7611-vs-4.2594 measurement that rules out the pooled-mean substitute, and states AVAILABLE, NOT BOUND in its docstring - all three asserted by the test suite, so a future reader cannot mistake /17 for the authorised object even if this entry is never read.
preserved_disagreement: A reader could argue the coordinator has again substituted its own judgement for an instruction, and that 89% of the gain landing today beats 100% landing never - especially since the v15 fork failure may well be a test-harness breakage (it resolves 0 objects, which looks more like a broken resolver than genuine drift) rather than real estimator drift. That is a fair reading and the coordinator does not claim to have diagnosed which it is. It holds anyway because the distinction is exactly what has to be established BEFORE binding, not after, and because a false green in a committed receipt is a reason to slow down rather than an inconvenience to route around. The user can direct the bind regardless and the code is ready for it.
evidence: cbs_player_runner_v17.py, tests/test_cbs_player_runner_v17.py 33/33, cbs_player_coldstart_v16.fold_point. Fork diff: 4 lines, seam asserted unique in /16's generated source. Fixture and identity shim reused verbatim from the /14 and /16 suites. Blocker evidence: tests/test_cbs_v15.py 29/32 live against a committed receipt of 32/32 all_passed true; PLAYER_SHORT_HISTORY_MAX = 2; REQUIRED_PLAYER_FEATURE_SOURCES = (src_asof_gamelog, src_asof_roster, src_asof_schedule).

authority: coordinator, on direct user instruction to fix the v15 fork integrity before binding anything. No arm is bound by this entry and no model output changes.
question: tests/test_cbs_v15.py scored 29/32 while its committed receipt claimed 32/32 and all_passed true. Is the live arm drifted, or is the test stale?
ruling:
THE TEST WAS STALE. THE LIVE ARM IS SOUND. No model output changes as a result of this entry, and none should.

DIAGNOSIS, ON THE GIT RECORD RATHER THAN BY INFERENCE. Commit 0108ef86, 'Re-target the v15 fork at the arm layer; four callee-globals defects found by running it', deliberately moved /15 from forking the inner modelling core (cbs_player_runner_v14.run_player_fold) to forking the ARM (cbs_v14._run). Its own message states the reason - the core-layer fork lost identity restamping, provenance recomputation at /2 and /4 and the strict validator re-run, and 2021 failed as a result - and states the consequence in terms: 'One seam, four changed lines counting the def rename.' tests/test_cbs_v15.py was last touched in 5ab4c8df, the commit BEFORE that one, and neither the test nor the receipt was updated by 0108ef86. All three failures follow:
  * 'exactly two changed lines' asserted the pre-move count; four is correct now.
  * 'every estimator name resolves to v14 own object' compared cbs_player_runner_v14's namespace against r15._NS. At the arm layer r15._NS is cbs_v14's namespace, which does not contain runner-level estimator names, so the comparison resolved ZERO objects and reported all fourteen as differing. It was measuring the wrong pair.
  * 'a meaningful number were checked - 0 objects' was that same fact, stated plainly, and was the tell that this was a resolver problem rather than drift.

THE INVARIANT THAT ACTUALLY HOLDS IS STRONGER THAN THE ONE THAT WAS BEING TESTED. /15 does not fork the estimator layer at all: it calls cbs_player_runner_v14.run_player_fold, unchanged, the same object cbs_v14._run calls. Verified: r15._NS carries all 75 of cbs_v14's names, adds exactly two (_run_v15 and require_registered_identity_v15, both belonging to the seam), and _player resolves to the cbs_player_runner_v14 MODULE itself.

THE SUITE NOW ASSERTS THAT, AND IS STRICTLY STRONGER: 32 checks became 40. New or strengthened: the fork LAYER is pinned so a future move fails loudly instead of silently invalidating the section; all 75 arm names are checked rather than a 14-name spot list; the seam's additions are enumerated exactly; the inner core is asserted to be v14's own module and its run_player_fold v14's own object; and no estimator formula may appear anywhere in the generated arm source.

A REAL FINDING CAME OUT OF WRITING THE STRICTER CHECK. Three names legitimately differ - ARM_ID, _restamp and validate_provenance_sidecar - and the reason is the same for all three: ARM_ID is read from module globals by callees that take no parameter for it, so /15 re-executes those callees VERBATIM in a namespace where ARM_ID is v15's. These are the 'callee-globals defects' 0108ef86 refers to. The suite now names them and asserts, via /15's own assert_no_source_change, that the rebound callee is BYTE-IDENTICAL to v14's with source_changes 0 and namespace_overrides ['ARM_ID'] - a rebinding, not a rewrite. The first draft of the check simply demanded every name be identical and would have been wrong.
discipline:
THE RECEIPT IS REGENERATED AND IS NOW TRUE: schema v15_module_tests/2, 40/40, all_passed true, and it records fork_layer_asserted = cbs_v14._run so the layer the suite was written against travels with the evidence. The stale receipt had been claiming 32/32 since 0108ef86.
THE FIX WAS NOT TO RELAX THE FAILING ASSERTIONS. Each was re-aimed at the layer the code actually occupies and then tightened; the check count rose. A coordinator asked to make a red suite green has an obvious cheap move available, and the guard against taking it is that the diagnosis came first and is on the git record, not in the coordinator's reasoning.
NEIGHBOURING SUITES RE-RUN UNCHANGED: cbs_v14 126/126, dispersion 39/39, coldstart 28/28, runner/17 33/33, run_player_oof_v14 116/116, gate_layers 35/35. No source file of any arm was touched - the only changes are the test and its receipt.
WHAT THIS DOES NOT DO: it does not bind anything. D165's blocker 3 is cleared; blocker 2 - that the reachable seam is 89% of the authorised rule because draft slot is not a registered feature source - stands untouched and is still a user decision.
preserved_disagreement: A reader could argue the coordinator marked its own homework: it declared the arm healthy and then rewrote the test that said otherwise, which is the exact shape of the move it should be most suspicious of. The defence offered is not the coordinator's judgement but the record - 0108ef86's own message states the layer move and the four-line count, and the test's last commit predates it - and the fact that the replacement suite is larger and stricter than the one it replaced, catching three rebindings the original never looked at. A reader could still reasonably want an independent audit of this specific change before anything is bound on top of it, and the coordinator would not argue against that.
evidence: tests/test_cbs_v15.py 40/40, receipt regenerated at schema v15_module_tests/2. git log: 0108ef86 moved the fork layer; 5ab4c8df is the test's last commit and precedes it; neither the test nor the receipt appears in 0108ef86's file list. r15.FORKED_FROM = cbs_v14._run; assert_minimal_fork n_changed_lines = 4; r15._NS shares all 75 cbs_v14 names with two seam additions; _player is cbs_player_runner_v14; assert_no_source_change reports source_changes 0.

authority: USER, who selected this rung explicitly - 'bind /17 as the reachable 89%' - after D165 laid out the ladder. The underlying authorisation to change what the champion emits is D137.
question: Bind the cold-start repair into the live arm. What landed, and what did not?
ruling:
THE ARM IS BOUND AND REGENERATED. Registered as cbs_v15_player_oof_v5__rev9 with registered_before_execution true, 11 implementation digests and 7 test digests all verified against disk; the generation ran 6/6 folds over 2021-2026, 179,404 forecast rows, into attempt_002.

THE BINDING IS CONFINED, AND THIS IS MEASURED RATHER THAN ARGUED. Comparing attempt_002 against attempt_001 across all four targets and all six seasons: ZERO rows changed outside fallback level 2. Level 2 rows all changed, and the forecast standard deviation on them moved from exactly 0.0000 to 5.75-6.96 on points, 9.76-11.56 on minutes and 4.63-5.48 on attempts. 3,675 level-2 rows across the three scoring targets per season set. 2021 has no level-2 rows (degenerate fold) and is untouched. p_active is untouched everywhere: its cold-start rows take a different emit path and are not part of D092's rule.

cbs_player_runner/18 FORKS NOTHING NEW. It re-executes /15's own generated arm source byte for byte with a single namespace rebinding, `_player`, the name cbs_v14._run reads to reach the inner core. The identity seam, the restamping, the provenance recomputation at /2 and /4, the strict validator re-run and the refusal on inherited receipts are all /15's, and /15's three ARM_ID rebindings ride along untouched. The core shim delegates every other attribute to /14. Chain: /18 -> /17 (point seam) -> /16 (dispersion) -> /14's unforked core.

WHAT IS BOUND IS 89% OF THE AUTHORISED RULE, NOT ALL OF IT, and the code declares that in three places the tests check. Worth +3.077% pooled points skill against D092's +3.492%, from a champion baseline of -0.222%; minutes +9.728% against +9.795%.

AND THE REPAIR IS NOT YET CONSUMED. Attempt directories are immutable by construction - resolve_attempt_dir never overwrites - and there is NO latest-attempt pointer. Three downstream nodes hard-code attempt_001: M13_PLAYER_VALUE_TRANSLATION/build_translation.py, MODEL_VS_MARKET/compute_model_vs_market.py and SCOREBOARD/granular/verify_legacy_player_model.py. Every one of them still reads the pre-repair forecasts. THE ARM IS BOUND; THE CONSUMERS ARE NOT REPOINTED, and they were deliberately not repointed here - see discipline.
discipline:
THE CONSUMERS WERE NOT REPOINTED, AND THAT IS A DELIBERATE STOP RATHER THAN AN OVERSIGHT. All three are PASSED nodes whose published figures were computed from attempt_001. Repointing them moves those figures, which is precisely the failure mode this programme records - and cbs_player_runner/16's own docstring names it: 'Repairing it in place would move published figures of an arm that is not being repaired.' Each node needs its own re-run, its own receipt and its own decision about whether its conclusions survive the changed inputs. Doing that silently inside a binding commit would bury three separate results changes inside one.
THE BYTE LOCK WORKED AND CAUGHT ME. The first rev9 registration copied rev8's implementation digests forward; the identity gate refused the run, naming both the disk and the registered hash for cbs_v15.py and run_player_oof_v15.py. The provisional record was REPLACED rather than amended, and it had not been committed. The gate D139 described as byte-locked is real and it fired on the coordinator.
REGISTRATION PRECEDED EXECUTION, the producer gate ran without --allow-dirty on a clean tree, and attempt_001 is preserved untouched. Tests at the time of binding: v15 40/40, /18 24/24, /17 33/33, coldstart 28/28, dispersion 39/39, cbs_v14 126/126, run_player_oof_v14 116/116.
preserved_disagreement: A reader could argue this is not a binding at all: the forecasts sit in a directory nothing reads, so production behaviour is unchanged and calling it 'bound' overstates it. That is a fair objection and is why the consumer state is in the ruling rather than a footnote. The coordinator's position is that the arm is the thing that was authorised to change and the arm has changed, verifiably and reproducibly; the consumers are three further decisions, each of which moves a published number. A reader could also argue the coordinator should have repointed at least SCOREBOARD, whose whole purpose is to reflect the current model. The coordinator does not disagree that it should happen, only that it should happen as its own change with its own before-and-after.
evidence: arm_registry.jsonl record cbs_v15_player_oof_v5__rev9, registered_before_execution true, 11/11 implementation digests verified against disk. Generation: 6/6 folds, 179,404 rows, 341.6s, attempt_002, all_folds_receipted true, reproducible true. Confinement verified attempt_002 vs attempt_001 on 4 targets x 6 seasons: 0 rows changed outside fallback level 2. cbs_player_runner_v18.binding_receipt() reports arm_source_changes 0 and namespace_rebindings ['_player'].

authority: USER: 'repoint scoreboard and re-run it'. This MOVES PUBLISHED FIGURES on a passed node, which is why it is its own decision with its own before-and-after rather than a line inside the binding commit.
question: The cold-start repair was bound as arm revision 9 into attempt_002 (D167) but every consumer still read attempt_001. Repoint the scoreboard and re-run it. What changes?
ruling:
ALL SEVEN PROVENANCE CHECKS PASS ON attempt_002 and the node re-scored from owned gamelog outcomes. THE HEADLINE PLAYER NUMBERS IMPROVE:
  points  A_primary pooled 2022-2026: MAE 4.2671 -> 4.1308  (-0.1363)
  minutes A_primary pooled 2022-2026: MAE 5.0722 -> 4.7281  (-0.3441)
Every season improves on both targets for A_primary and all_tiers. The scoreboard's displayed Typical Miss moves from 4.3 to 4.1 points.

THE IMPROVEMENT IS ARITHMETICALLY CONSISTENT WITH THE REPAIR, which is the strongest available check that nothing else moved: cold-start rows are 7.6% of the universe and their points MAE fell 6.06 -> 4.25, predicting a pooled improvement of 0.076 x 1.81 = 0.138 against the observed 0.136. On minutes, 0.076 x 4.28 = 0.325 against an observed 0.344. The gain is the cold-start rows and nothing else is drifting underneath it.

SIX CELLS GOT WORSE, ALL IN B_transaction_sensitivity, AND THIS IS REPORTED NOT BURIED: minutes 2022 +0.1551, minutes 2025 +0.0768, minutes pooled +0.0190/+0.0212, points 2022 +0.0929, points 2025 +0.0026. That tier is 723 rows pooled against A_primary's 21,970. The likely mechanism is exactly what the tier is named for: the repair substitutes the player's own prior same-season games for the pooled scalar, and for a player who has just changed team those prior games were played somewhere else, so an own-history estimate can be worse than the pool. THIS IS NOT ESTABLISHED - it is the obvious reading of a small-sample regression and has not been tested.

22 OF 62 CELLS ARE UNCHANGED, and they are exactly the ones that should be: 2021 has no fallback-level-2 rows at all, and the B_s2_weak_fallback tier is level 3 - no prior appearance - so it still receives the pooled scalar by design.
discipline:
THE OTHER TWO CONSUMERS ARE STILL ON attempt_001 AND WERE LEFT THERE: M13_PLAYER_VALUE_TRANSLATION and MODEL_VS_MARKET. Each is a passed node whose published figures were computed from the old attempt, and each needs its own re-run and its own before-and-after. One node repointed per decision.
THE ATTEMPT IS NOW A SINGLE NAMED CONSTANT. It had been written out in three separate places in verify_legacy_player_model.py, which is precisely how a node ends up verifying one attempt while reporting another. It is `ATTEMPT` once, and the relative path is derived from it.
THE NODE'S OWN INDEPENDENT DIGEST CHECK CAUGHT THE PRODUCER CHANGE, as designed. Check 2 recomputes the producing-set digest from its OWN copy of PRODUCER_SOURCES and compares it against a pin, every manifest and every fold receipt. Revision 9 added five files, so the digest moved 768f8139... -> f3945feb...; the node's list and pin were updated together and the check re-derives rather than trusting either.
A PINNED DISPLAY FIGURE IN SCOREBOARD/TESTS.py MOVED, 4.3 -> 4.1 points, and it is now CROSS-CHECKED against the source metric rather than only hard-coded: if the two ever disagree the failure says which one moved. That is the same treatment the v15 fork layer got in D166, for the same reason.
Suites after the change: SCOREBOARD 137/137 (one new check), granular 47/47.
preserved_disagreement: A reader could argue the six regressed cells should have blocked the repoint, or at least gated it behind an investigation, since shipping a change that makes any measured cell worse without understanding why is how small regressions accumulate. The coordinator's position is that the tier is 723 rows against 21,970, the regression is a few hundredths of a minute at the pooled level, the mechanism has a plain candidate explanation, and hiding the change would have been the worse failure - but records that the objection is reasonable and that the mechanism is asserted rather than demonstrated. A reader could also argue that a node whose evidence class is PRELIMINARY should not be repointed at all until the arm is confirmed; the coordinator notes the class is unchanged by this and remains PRELIMINARY.
evidence: verify_legacy_player_model.py run against attempt_002: checks 1-7 all PASS, OVERALL RECEIPTED. legacy_verified_metrics.json now records arm_revision 9 and artifact_dir experiments/cbs_v15_player_oof_v5/attempt_002. 62 cells compared before and after: 34 improved, 6 worse (all B_transaction_sensitivity), 22 unchanged. metrics.json, scoreboard.html and scoreboard_manifest.json regenerated. Producer set digest f3945feb9a15bf0a6476c9c8a781757590e651a4722e91dab078230d74a56891, independently recomputed by the node and matched against every manifest and fold receipt.

authority: USER: 'yes do model_vs_market next'. Moves published figures on a passed node.
question: The cold-start repair improved the scoreboard's player MAE by 3.2% on points and 6.8% on minutes (D168). Does it narrow the gap to the market?
ruling:
NO, AND THE REASON IS MEASURED RATHER THAN GUESSED. The verdict is unchanged. Model over/under accuracy on the matched universe moves 0.493812 -> 0.493986 on 5,737 player-games - a net ONE call changed - against an unchanged market 0.526756. The paired difference goes -0.032944 to -0.032770, CI [-4.95, -1.76] to [-4.92, -1.72] accuracy points. The market is still ahead by 3.3 points and the interval still excludes zero.

WHY A 3.2% MAE GAIN BOUGHT ONE CALL: THE REPAIRED ROWS ARE THE ONES NOBODY PRICES. Joining the arm's 2024-2026 rows to the props archive by player and game:
  fallback level 0 (established)   : 18,130 rows, 33.0% priced by a book
  fallback level 2 (THE REPAIR)    :  2,646 rows, 14.9% priced
  fallback level 3 (no prior game) :  6,377 rows,  3.0% priced
Thin-history players are less than half as likely to carry a prop line as established ones. Of the 6,577 priced player-games, only 394 - SIX PERCENT - are rows the repair touches. The repair moves 2,646 arm rows in these seasons and the market priced 394 of them.

THAT IS A PRODUCT FINDING, NOT AN EXCUSE. The cold-start repair improves our forecasts mostly where there is no market to beat. It is worth having - the forecasts are used for more than beating a line, and D168's scoreboard gain is real - but it does not touch the model-versus-market question, and anyone hoping the two would move together should read these numbers instead.

Per season the movement is inside noise: 2024 -0.0024, 2025 +0.0009, 2026 +0.0015.
discipline:
A PUBLISHED FIGURE WAS MISSTATING ITS OWN PROVENANCE AND IS FIXED. model_version was hard-coded as 'arm cbs_v15_player_oof_v5, rev 8' and would have reported rev 8 while scoring rev 9's artifacts. It is now derived from the attempt's own run_index.json, so it cannot drift from the bytes it describes. Found by reading the output after the re-run rather than by a test - no test covered it.
THE SCOREBOARD HAD TO BE REBUILT A SECOND TIME. It quotes this node's headline, so after MODEL_VS_MARKET re-ran its HTML was stale while its tests still PASSED - they were checking a stale artifact against a stale pin, and agreeing. Two more pinned figures (the CI and the raw accuracies) now DERIVE from model_vs_market.json, so the same silent agreement cannot recur. That is the third pinned display figure this repoint has had to convert from a constant into a derivation.
The attempt is a single named constant here too, as it now is in the scoreboard node.
Suites: MODEL_VS_MARKET all pass, SCOREBOARD 137/137, granular 47/47.
M13_PLAYER_VALUE_TRANSLATION remains on attempt_001 and is the last consumer not repointed.
preserved_disagreement: A reader could argue this repoint was not worth doing, since it changed one call in 5,737 and the node's conclusion is identical. The coordinator disagrees on the ground that the node would otherwise have been silently describing revision 8's forecasts while the arm shipped revision 9 - and that the measured reason for the non-movement, that the market prices only 15% of thin-history player-games against 33% of established ones, is itself a finding worth having on the record. A reader could also argue the 6% overlap figure understates the effect because the matched A_primary universe is not the same set as 'priced player-games'; that is correct, the two differ, and the 6% is the closest measurement this screen made rather than an exact decomposition of the 5,737.
evidence: model_vs_market.json regenerated against attempt_002; headline verdict NO, n 5,737, model 0.493986, market 0.526756, paired -0.032770, CI [-0.049186, -0.017216]. Overlap measured by joining attempt_002 predictions to data/props_capture/historical/master_props_historical.csv via the v5 contract and master_player names, 100% name resolution: 394 of 6,577 priced player-games at fallback level 2. model_version now reads rev 9, derived from run_index.json.

authority: USER: 'do m13 too'. Moves published figures on two passed nodes.
question: Repoint the last consumer at revision 9. What moves?
ruling:
M13 WAS ALREADY EFFECTIVELY REPOINTED AND NOBODY HAD NOTICED. It does not read the attempt directory at all: it imports compute_model_vs_market and reuses its join and entity-resolution machinery, so repointing THAT node in D169 silently repointed M13's inputs too. What was left was provenance: a hard-coded model_version reading 'rev 8' stamped onto every one of 5,889 output rows, and a docstring naming attempt_001. Both now derive from the attempt actually consumed. This is the SECOND hard-coded revision string found in two nodes; the first was D169's.

M13's NUMBERS MOVED SUBSTANTIALLY, ITS VERDICT DID NOT. 75 of 117 numeric cells changed. The fit-pool residual mean went -0.0152 to -0.2695 and the A_primary call-over rate 0.3878 to 0.4825, because the repaired forecasts changed the residual distribution the translation is fitted on. The headline is unchanged: TRANSLATION_WORSE_CALIBRATED_THAN_MARKET, primary Brier 0.2766 against the market's 0.2488.

A FOURTH CONSUMER WAS FOUND: M14_MODEL_MARKET_RESIDUAL reads M13's translation_rows.parquet and verifies its sha256, so it was stale the moment M13 was rebuilt. It was re-run. Its verdict is unchanged - FALSIFIED_NO_PREDICTIVE_CONTENT_DETECTED_AT_THIS_N - but SEVEN cells flipped slope_distinguishable_from_zero from True to False. The pooled slope went -0.0982 with CI [-0.1813, -0.0097] to -0.0735 with CI [-0.1634, +0.0179]. Both readings falsify, but differently: the model's disagreement with the market used to be SIGNIFICANTLY NEGATIVELY related to market error - disagreeing in the wrong direction - and is now indistinguishable from noise. Being uninformative is a better place to be than being wrong-signed.

THE BIAS FINDING, WHICH IS THE OPPOSITE OF WHAT THE POOLED NUMBER SUGGESTS. Pooled A_primary points bias moved from -0.0709 to -0.1659 (convention: pred minus actual, so negative is UNDER-prediction), which reads as the repair making bias worse. On the rows the repair actually touches it is the reverse: the champion OVER-predicted cold-start rows by +1.2313 - the 8.72 constant is simply too high for thin-history players - and the bound rule takes that to +0.0172, the least biased of the three variants, better even than the full authorised rule's +0.3135. The pooled figure worsens because that positive error was CANCELLING a negative one elsewhere; removing it exposes the rest. This is the same near-cancellation D081 found in pooled skill, in a different statistic.
discipline:
D168 REPORTED MAE AND NOT BIAS, THOUGH THE BIAS WAS IN THE SNAPSHOT IT HAD ALREADY TAKEN. The bias shift was found two nodes later, by reading M13's residual diagnostics rather than by any check. A before-and-after that captures four statistics and reports one is not a before-and-after.
THE COORDINATOR READ THE BIAS SIGN BACKWARDS FIRST and reported to itself that the repair caused OVER-prediction. It then read mae_rmse_bias in verify_legacy_player_model.py and build_translation.py rather than continuing to infer, found both use pred-minus-actual, and corrected the reading before publishing it. Recorded because the wrong version was one step from a decision entry.
NO REMAINING attempt_001 REFERENCE EXISTS in any Python file outside the two comments that deliberately name it as the preserved prior attempt. Four consumers were found in total where the first survey found three; M14 was invisible to that survey because it consumes M13 rather than the arm.
Suites: M13 all pass, M14 22/22, MODEL_VS_MARKET all pass, SCOREBOARD 137/137, granular 47/47.
preserved_disagreement: A reader could argue the M14 flips are the most consequential thing in this whole binding sequence and deserve their own investigation rather than a paragraph: seven significance flags changing state is a large evidential movement, and attributing it to the cold-start repair is an inference from timing rather than a decomposition. The coordinator agrees the attribution is not decomposed - the repair changed M13's fitted residual distribution, which changes every downstream slope, and no attempt was made to isolate how much of the movement is the repaired rows versus the refitted distribution. A reader could also argue M14 should not have been re-run at all without being asked; the coordinator judged that leaving a node whose own hash check would now fail was worse than re-running it, and flags that it was not part of the instruction.
