authority: coordinator, on direct user instruction to fix the O16 warning. No node status changed, no event was added, and no human gate was reopened or closed.
question: validate_graph.py warned 'O16_SHARED_SCHEMA_ADOPTION: seed status USER_REQUIRED vs derived PASSED'. Was a human gate bypassed, or was the check wrong?
ruling:
NEITHER THE GATE NOR THE DATA WAS AT FAULT. THE WARNING WAS STRUCTURAL AND COULD NOT HAVE MEANT ANYTHING. D022 records the user approving all three operations bundles in chat on 2026-08-06, its nodes field names O16, and the node_passed event says 'Human gate closed by user authorization D022'. The gate was satisfied and the node genuinely passed.

THE TWO RULES ARE JOINTLY UNSATISFIABLE. validate_node_contract REQUIRES a human_gate node to carry seed status USER_REQUIRED. derive_state gives an event-forced status PRECEDENCE over the human_gate rule. So the moment such a node legitimately passes, its seed and derived statuses diverge BY CONSTRUCTION and stay diverged for the life of the graph. The first repair attempted here - setting O16's seed to PASSED - was refused by the node contract, which is how the structural nature of it was discovered.

SO THE CHECK IS AMENDED, NOT THE DATA. Check 6 now judges the thing that matters: whether the event that produced the node's current status cites a ledger decision that EXISTS and NAMES THAT NODE. A human gate closed with a recorded authority is silent; one closed without is an ERROR. The check is strictly stronger than what it replaced, which fired identically whether the gate had been satisfied or bypassed and therefore told a reader nothing either way.

O16 was the ONLY node affected. 96 nodes diverge seed-from-derived, and the other 95 are seeded READY or BLOCKED, both in DERIVED_ONLY, which is the intended behaviour for a graph that moves. USER_REQUIRED was deliberately NOT added to DERIVED_ONLY: that would have silenced the one class where a divergence is worth stopping for.
discipline:
THE TAMPER TEST CAUGHT THIS COORDINATOR TWICE, AND BOTH VERSIONS WOULD HAVE SHIPPED A CHECK THAT COULD NOT FIRE.
  v1 accepted any D-number appearing anywhere in the event. Stripping O16's real authority still passed, because the same sentence mentions D017 - an unrelated push authorisation whose nodes field is null. A regex over free text is not an authority check.
  v2 required the decision to exist AND name the node, which fixed that, and STILL passed the tamper test - because it scanned every status-forcing event, and `agent_launched` also forces a status (RUNNING) and cites D022 in its own detail. The authority was being read from an event that did not close anything.
  v3 reads only the event whose mapped status EQUALS the derived status - the event that actually closed the gate. Tamper test: stripping D022 from node_passed now FAILS with 'a gate closed by nobody is not a closed gate'; restoring it passes. Clean tree: 108 nodes, 0 errors, 0 warnings.
A quieter check that cannot fire is worse than the noisy one it replaces, and the only reason this one is not that is that it was tested against tampering three times rather than reasoned about once. GRAPH_EVENTS.jsonl and PROGRAM_GRAPH.json were restored byte-identical after each test; the only file changed by this decision is validate_graph.py.
preserved_disagreement: A reader could argue the coordinator has again loosened a check that was flagging its own work as suspicious, and that the honest move was to leave the warning and let a human judge it. The defence is that the warning was provably uninformative - it fires for every satisfied human gate forever, by construction, and O16 is currently the only human_gate node that has passed, so the check had exactly one subject and no discriminating power over it. A reader could also argue the new rule is too permissive in a different way: any decision naming the node counts, so a coordinator could self-author a decision and cite it. That is true and is NOT closed by this change - the ledger records who made each decision and under what authority, and nothing here verifies that a human, rather than a coordinator, supplied it.

O16 events: agent_launched (RUNNING), agent_returned (VERIFYING), node_passed (PASSED, cites D022). validate_graph.py check 6 amended; tamper test fails on a stripped citation and passes on restore. authority: coordinator, on the user's direct question 'is there any profitable strat yet?'. Market prices and owned gamelog outcomes only; no fitted model appears in this node, so S42 is untouched. SHADOW unchanged; nothing is authorised to be staked.
question: Every profitability figure this programme holds is measured against CONSENSUS. Do the quotes that beat consensus actually WIN?
ruling:
NO. THE ONE CANDIDATE STRATEGY LOSES MONEY AND THE LOSS IS SIGNIFICANT.

On 19,559 book-quotes with realised outcomes across 648 games, 230 game dates, 9 books and seasons 2024-2026, cluster-bootstrapped by game date:
  every quote indiscriminately        -4.97%  [-5.88, -3.96]   win 50.2%  mean price -72.3
  beats peer consensus (edge > 0)     -8.99%  [-15.53, -1.77]  win 45.3%  mean price +27.7
  gap 0-1pp                           -5.56%
  gap 1-2pp                           -4.25%
  gap 2-3pp                           -2.94%
  gap >= 3pp  [M30's ACT threshold]   -7.21%  [-12.93, -1.73]  win 47.2%  mean price +1.8
The threshold the board was built around loses 7.2 cents per dollar and its interval EXCLUDES ZERO. It is not unproven; it is measurably losing, and losing worse than betting at random. Selecting on edge > 0 is worse still at -8.99%.

THE MECHANISM IS VISIBLE IN ONE COLUMN. Mean price overall is -72.3; at gap >= 3pp it is +1.8. Selecting quotes where a book is generous relative to its peers is in practice SELECTING PLUS-MONEY LONGSHOT SIDES, which win 47.2% at roughly even money.

THE CONTROL INVERTS THE THESIS. Betting the OPPOSITE side of the same 3pp quotes - the side the peers call overpriced - returns -6.04% against the primary's -7.21%. Both lose, because vig is paid either way, but the side consensus calls underpriced does WORSE. The signal points the wrong way.

D157 IS NOT WRONG AND IS NOW BOUNDED. Its +1.44%/+2.74% is measured against CONSENSUS and replicated on 121,000 quotes; a dislocated quote really does revert toward its peers. Reverting toward consensus is not being right. This node is the first time the programme checked the second thing, and the two measurements disagree in sign.

SO THE ANSWER TO THE USER'S QUESTION IS NO, AND THIS CLOSES THE LAST CANDIDATE. Arbitrage is single-digit dollars a season (D153); line shopping removes 24.3% of vig and still returns -2.05% (D155/D157); middles are negative at the observed windows even with the push branch priced (D156); the model loses to the market and the cold-start repair did not narrow it (D141/D150/D169); consensus dislocation is this node. PROMOTIONS ARE THE ONLY ROUTE NEVER MEASURED, and they are unmeasured only because no real offer has been entered.
discipline:
THE COORDINATOR PUBLISHED THE UNTESTED VERSION OF THIS FIRST, AND THAT IS THE DEFECT WORTH RECORDING. D157's consensus-relative figure was relayed to the user as 'the only positive-expectation route measured', sized at 26-92 bets a season at +1% to +3%, with the caveat 'measured against consensus, not truth' attached. The caveat was correct and was carried as boilerplate through four exchanges rather than treated as the open question it was. It took the user asking directly whether anything was profitable for it to be tested. A caveat that never becomes a screen is decoration.
THE PREREGISTERED NEGATIVE CONTROL WAS EMPTY BY CONSTRUCTION. `gap` is defined on the side taken and the side taken is always the generous one, so `gap <= -3pp` could never contain a row. Had the primary come back positive, this screen would have reported a passing control that tested nothing. Substituted with the opposite side of the same quotes and disclosed.
THE PIPELINE IS VALIDATED BY ITS OWN BASELINE: betting every quote returns -4.97%, which is the vig this archive carries. A pipeline that could not reproduce the vig would not be trusted to measure a deviation from it.
P1 PASS, P2 FAIL, P3 FAIL, P4 FAIL, P5 PASS, P6 PASS-on-wording. P4 is the instructive one: the coordinator predicted the interval would include zero, i.e. that the sample was too small to conclude. It excludes zero, on the losing side.
preserved_disagreement: A reader could argue this node proves less than it claims: the archive holds ONE vendor-asserted snapshot per game at a median 1.16 hours before tip, its timestamp is unwitnessed (D027), and a signal measured on prices nobody could demonstrably have taken is not the signal a live board would trade. That is fair, and the negative result is evidence rather than closure - a faster feed or closing-line data could say otherwise. The coordinator's position is that the burden has now moved: the programme may no longer describe consensus dislocation as positive expectation without first showing it wins somewhere, and 'the archive is imperfect' is not that showing. A reader could also argue 915 quotes is too thin to overturn a 121,000-quote replication; the two measure different responses, so the larger sample does not adjudicate the smaller one's question.

authority: coordinator, on the user's question 'how can our model be improved, what is holding it back vs the market'. E0-style diagnostic, NON-CLAIMING, no evidence-ladder label sought. No wager-shaped claim; S42 untouched.
question: The programme knows THAT the market wins (D141, D150, D169). It has never decomposed WHY. Points are minutes x rate -- which one is losing?
ruling:
IT IS ENTIRELY MINUTES, AND THE SCORING-RATE MODEL IS ALREADY GOOD ENOUGH. On 5,889 matched player-games actually played, 2024-2026, cluster-bootstrapped by game date:
  MARKET implied mean                      MAE 4.9168 [4.816, 5.011]
  OUR MODEL as shipped                     MAE 5.2261 [5.113, 5.347]
  ours + ORACLE MINUTES, our own rate      MAE 4.5907 [4.493, 4.692]
The gap is +0.3093 points. Hand the model the realised minutes, change nothing else, and it lands 0.326 AHEAD of the market. The rate model is not what loses.

THE REQUIREMENT IS A 40% CUT IN MINUTES ERROR. Shrinking the minutes error toward truth and recomputing: parity with the market arrives at a shrink factor of 0.6, i.e. minutes MAE falling from 4.2070 to about 2.5242.

THAT WILL NOT COME FROM MODELLING AND THE PROGRAMME'S OWN RECORD SAYS SO. The entire reference ladder moved minutes MAE 5.272 -> 4.860, about 8%, and the richer blend was worse at 4.870. E1_I0053 tested eight context candidates and SEVEN WERE NULL, with tuning beating every one by 2.5-7.6x. E1_I0061 found per-row scale modelling of minutes uncertainty negative, twice. A 40% cut is roughly FIVE TIMES everything the modelling programme has ever achieved on this target.

SO IT IS AN INFORMATION GAP, AND THE MISSING INFORMATION IS IDENTIFIED. The production arm's registered feature sources are src_asof_gamelog, src_asof_roster and src_asof_schedule. The string 'injury' appears ZERO times in cbs_player_runner_v14.py, cbs_v7.py and cbs_v8.py. THE ARM HAS NEVER READ AN INJURY REPORT. Meanwhile data/injury_official_live holds 841 files and 86.2 MB of official league quarter-hour injury reports, injury_snapshots.csv, status_transitions.csv and the captured source PDFs. It is being collected daily and is wired into nothing that forecasts.

WHERE THE LOSS SITS, by realised minutes played: <12 min -0.0266 (we are LEVEL with the market), 12-20 +0.2242, 20-28 +0.3190, 28+ +0.3266. We lose on rotation regulars, where minutes are largest and a minutes error is most expensive in points.
discipline:
THE ORACLE ARMS CHEAT BY CONSTRUCTION AND ARE LABELLED AS INSTRUMENTS, NOT FORECASTS, in the module docstring, the report and here. Handing a model the realised minutes is not a forecast and no number in the oracle rows may be quoted as achievable.
WHAT THE COMPARISON DOES NOT SHOW: that our rate model beats the market's rate model. The market's 4.9168 already carries the market's OWN minutes uncertainty. The finding is that minutes uncertainty costs US more than the entire gap, not that we out-model the market on efficiency. The report states this in its own limitations rather than leaving the stronger reading available.
The minutes-played table conditions on a REALISED quantity and is descriptive only; it cannot be used to select rows prospectively.
WIRING INJURIES IN IS NOT AUTHORISED BY THIS ENTRY AND IS NOT FREE. It adds a registered feature source to a byte-locked arm, which is a contract change requiring a new arm revision and a generation run. Every row would need point-in-time discipline: an injury file reflecting CURRENT status rather than status at the forecast cutoff is a leak, and this programme has been bitten by exactly that class twice - D138's invisible sources and D151's re-stamped last_update, where 99.6% of captures looked fresh while 82.6% of prices were unchanged.
preserved_disagreement: A reader could argue the oracle-minutes result is close to tautological: minutes are the larger multiplicative term, so of course fixing them helps most, and the diagnostic tells us nothing we could not have reasoned out. The coordinator disagrees on two grounds - the SIZE was not predictable (that our existing rate model would land 0.326 AHEAD of the market was not obvious, and the alternative reading, that the market simply prices scoring better, was live until measured), and the 40% requirement converts a vague 'improve minutes' into a number that can be checked against what the programme has actually achieved. A reader could also argue the injury tape is being oversold: nobody has measured how much of the residual minutes error it would explain, and the answer could be very little. That is correct and untested. This entry identifies the largest UNUSED asset aimed at the binding constraint; it does not claim to know what it is worth.
evidence: 5,889 matched player-games, 260 game dates, cluster bootstrap 2000 draws seed 20260821. Market implied mean via MARKET_IMPLIED_PROJECTIONS/implied_mean.py; outcomes via mvm.load_outcomes(); minutes forecasts from attempt_002 predictions__e_minutes_given_active. Minutes MAE 4.2070 against actual sd 6.4313. REQUIRED_PLAYER_FEATURE_SOURCES verified in cbs_v8.py:97; zero 'injury' matches in the runner and core. injury_official_live: 841 files, 86.2 MB.

authority: coordinator, on the user's instruction to run the screen D173 proposed. Feasibility measurement on ten game dates; no evidence-ladder label sought. S42 untouched, SHADOW unchanged, no fitted scoring model in the node.
question: D173 named the official injury tape as the largest unused asset aimed at the minutes gap. What is it actually worth, point-in-time?
ruling:
THREE FINDINGS, AND THE FIRST IS STRUCTURAL AND WAS INVISIBLE UNTIL THE POINT-IN-TIME JOIN WAS DONE PROPERLY.

1. UNDER THE MODEL'S OWN FORECAST CUTOFF THE TAPE DOES NOT EXIST. At 18:00 UTC the day before the game - the contract's convention - status is available on 0.0% of rows. NOT ONE. The reports are published on game day; the earliest capture for a game arrives roughly nine hours AFTER the cutoff the arm must respect. So 'wire the injury tape into the minutes model' is not a data-source change, it is a FORECAST-CUTOFF change, which is a far larger contract question than adding an input.

2. IT IS A NEAR-PERFECT AVAILABILITY SIGNAL. At the latest pre-tip capture: Out n=40 -> 0.0% appeared, perfectly separating; Available n=23 -> 95.7%; not-listed n=631 -> 85.7%. Coverage is 10% of rows because the report lists designated players only, and not being listed is itself the common case.

3. IT IS WORTH NOTHING FOR MINUTES GIVEN THE PLAYER PLAYED. On the 568 appeared rows, with a per-status offset fitted walk-forward on strictly earlier dates: BASE 4.6955, BASE+A 4.6933 (+0.0022), BASE+B 4.7059 (-0.0104). Knowing a player is Questionable or Probable does not predict how long they play once they do play. It slightly hurts.

SO D173'S RECOMMENDATION SPLITS AND ONLY HALF SURVIVES. M33 established the model-market gap is entirely MINUTES-GIVEN-PLAYED and named this tape as the asset aimed at it. On this sample the tape does not touch that quantity at all. It is aimed at the AVAILABILITY branch - a real and separate win that E1_I0062 already sized at 17.8% on prop-shaped questions. The coordinator's message to the user implied the tape was pointed at the minutes gap; on this evidence it is not.
discipline:
THE SCREEN COULD NOT USE THE SHIPPED ARM AND SAYS SO. The frozen outcome snapshot the market nodes read ends 2026-07-31; the injury capture begins 2026-08-06. THEY DO NOT OVERLAP ON A SINGLE ROW. The raw gamelogs are current to 2026-08-20, so the screen rebuilt the ladder's tuned-EWMA baseline rather than wait for an arm regeneration - and its numbers are therefore comparable to R2_EWMA_TUNED, not to the arm.
TEN GAME DATES IS NOT EVIDENCE and the prereg said so before the numbers existed. P4 was committed in advance: no interval separates from base, and a screen this size returning a significant result should be doubted rather than believed. Out at n=40 and Questionable at n=5 are not samples to build on.
THE TWO CUTOFFS ARE REPORTED SEPARATELY AND NEITHER MAY STAND IN FOR THE OTHER. A result under the latest-pre-tip cutoff measures a different product with a different information set and may never be quoted as an improvement to the current model. That separation was frozen in the prereg, not chosen after seeing which one looked better.
The ET-to-UTC conversion is a fixed -4 offset, correct for this single August window and wrong in general; recorded rather than generalised.
preserved_disagreement: A reader could argue the minutes null is an artefact of coverage rather than a finding: only 10% of rows carry any status at all, and the offset for the informative categories is fitted on a handful of rows, so the screen may simply lack the data to see an effect that is there. That is correct and the coordinator does not claim otherwise - P4 was preregistered for exactly this reason. What the screen DOES establish independently of sample size is finding 1, which is arithmetic rather than statistical: zero rows carry a status before the contract cutoff, and no amount of additional capture changes that without moving the cutoff. A reader could also argue the cutoff is ours to choose and the whole objection dissolves; the coordinator agrees it is a live option and notes it would change what every existing receipted figure means.
evidence: PREREG.md sha256 0fcdb68a2db87707a2ed6b36fca8fd4e22adf929a2a7410419fee1fe5804c3db. 701 player-game rows, 10 dates (2026-08-06..08-20 with the 08-10..08-14 blackout), 29 games, 198 players. injury_snapshots.csv 10,715 rows over 786 captures. CUTOFF_A coverage 0.0%, CUTOFF_B 10.0%. Minutes on 568 appeared rows, cluster bootstrap by game date, 2000 draws, seed 20260821. P1 PASS, P2 FAIL, P3 n/a, P4 PASS.

authority: USER: '1, 2, 3 go for it' - authorising the three follow-ups D174 proposed. E0-style diagnostic, non-claiming, ten game dates. S42 untouched, SHADOW unchanged, no fitted scoring model in the node.
question: (1) Can the forecast cutoff move? (2) Is the injury tape worth wiring into p_active rather than minutes? (3) Is the capture still running?
ruling:
1. THE CUTOFF ALREADY MOVES, AND THIS CORRECTS M34. The contract applies TWO policies, not one: date_only_prior_day_cutoff on 32,243 rows (71.9%) at 18:00 UTC the day before, and exact_tip_T-90m on 12,608 rows (28.1%) at ninety minutes before tip, ON GAME DAY. M34's finding that the tape is visible on 0.0% of rows is CORRECT FOR THE DATE-ONLY POLICY AND WRONG AS A BLANKET STATEMENT; M34 could not reach the contract (its outcome snapshot ends 2026-07-31, before the capture begins) and applied the documented fallback to every row.

WHAT DECIDES THE POLICY IS EVIDENCE, NOT PERMISSION. resolve_tip_times admits a tip only from an observation recorded strictly before that observation's OWN reported tip minus 90 minutes - point-in-time, fail-closed. Its only sources today are odds_extension (12,550) and props_historical (58). Everything else falls back because no qualifying tip observation exists, not because a later cutoff is disallowed.

AND THE INJURY CAPTURE IS ITSELF A QUALIFYING SOURCE. Each capture records game_time_et alongside retrieval_ts_utc. 26 of 31 matchup-dates (83.9%) carry a qualifying observation, with a MEDIAN LEAD OF 22.8 HOURS before tip. The tape does not merely need a later cutoff - it supplies the evidence that would make one legal.

2. AT T-90m THE TAPE BECOMES LEGIBLE AND IS WORTH 15.2% ON AVAILABILITY. Status visible on 0.0% of rows under date-only against 9.3% under T-90m. Appearance by status: Out n=33 6.1%, Doubtful n=1 0%, Questionable n=11 63.6%, Probable n=17 94.1%, Available n=3 100%, not listed n=636 85.1%. Walk-forward Brier on appearance, per-status rates fitted on strictly earlier dates only, scored on 627 rows: 0.15090 -> 0.12801, +15.2%.

3. THE CAPTURE IS RUNNING AND NEEDED NOTHING. 903 captures, 2026-08-06 19:41 to 2026-08-21 17:57 UTC, 192 in the last 48 hours, WNBA_InjuryCapture and WNBA_InjuryLive both Ready.

THE ROUTE IS NOW SPECIFIC: admit injury captures as a tip-time observation source, which lifts games to T-90m; at T-90m consume the status in p_active. IT DOES NOT CLOSE THE MARKET GAP - M33's deficit is minutes among players who play, and M34 showed the tape does nothing for that.
discipline:
A FIRST PASS AT THE BRIER USED HAND-CHOSEN CONSTANTS (Out -> 0, listed -> 0.95) and returned +16.7%. That is in-sample flattery dressed as a measurement. It was refitted walk-forward with per-status rates from strictly earlier game dates only, and the finding survives at +15.2%. The weaker number is the one recorded.
THE E1_I0062 COMPARISON IS DELIBERATELY NOT MADE. That screen measured the shipped p_active at 17.8% on a prop-shaped THRESHOLD question against a different baseline. The two numbers are not on the same scale and must not be added or ranked; the report says so where a reader would be tempted.
THE 83.9% TIP-OBSERVATION FIGURE IS OVER MATCHUP-DATES THE TAPE COVERS, which are by construction game-days with reports. Whether it extends to the full schedule is untested and is recorded as untested.
TEN GAME DATES, 701 ROWS, Out AT n=33. Nothing here generalises, and the ET-to-UTC conversion is a fixed -4 offset correct only for this August window.
preserved_disagreement: A reader could argue the coordinator has now corrected its own headline twice in three entries - D173 pointed the tape at minutes, D174 said it was unusable at the cutoff, and D175 says the cutoff is not what D174 described - and that the underlying problem is a habit of publishing a finding before checking the structure it depends on. That is a fair characterisation and the coordinator does not dispute it: each correction came from looking at something that could have been looked at first. A reader could also argue that moving the cutoff is a much larger change than this entry makes it sound, since every receipted figure in the programme was computed under the current policy mix; the coordinator agrees and has put that in the report's limitations rather than the recommendation.

authority: GRAPH_POLICY s5; M00 contract; D023 amendment 4; node acceptance criteria
question: M03_CAPTURE_UPGRADE was the only READY node with no outputs. Its acceptance criteria include the D023 amendment-4 timestamp requirement, which is the same defect M36 s02 measured in the live props capture. Are its seven acceptance criteria met, and may it close?

All seven criteria met: (1) cadence measured per era (60.0 min before 2026-08-19, 5.0 after, 524 captures over 23.1 days) with real credit arithmetic -- 3,407 credits/30d, 3.41% of the D029 tier -- and games/day MEASURED at mean 2.91 max 6 rather than assumed at 5.0, which would have been 72% too high; (2) event-driven bursts specified against the existing injury/news first-seen triggers with a costed 23,000 credit/month budget; (3) the five mandatory timing fields specified at schema level, adopting the pattern the INJURY capture already implements correctly rather than inventing one; (4) no-backdating enforced by a monotone first_seen and a payload digest that excludes timing fields, tamper-tested; (5) nothing needs paid quota, so NO USER_REQUIRED purchase line item is raised to M02B; (6) no in-flight draft existed to reconcile, so the node's artifacts are original and no duplication occurred; (7) additive and reversible -- legacy columns keep names and positions, and NO running capture script is modified, deployment being outside this node's write scope. TESTS.py 32/32 with every invariant tamper-tested (3 tampers, 6 failures produced). TWO LIMITS RECORDED, NOT REPAIRED: the coverage tail (4 of 58 games, 6.9%, with zero captures inside T-24h) is the D154 machine-uptime constraint and no cadence or schema change addresses it; and the new fields exist only from deployment, so every archived row keeps the weaker single stamp and historical timing claims must still carry that limitation. A FINDING AROSE FROM A BUG: grouping games on exact commence_time split single games and produced a false 35.2% zero-coverage figure; measured properly, 43 of 58 games (74.1%) have a REVISED tip time, median 5 min max 30, which vindicates resolve_tip_times comparing against the tip as reported at each moment. Deployment of the schema into the running captures is NOT authorised by this ruling and remains a separate scoped act.

authority: GRAPH_POLICY s5; M00 contract; D024 SHADOW default; S42 CLOSED; node acceptance criteria
question: M23_SHADOW_TRADING was READY. Are its four acceptance criteria met, and may it close -- given that M22 has already measured every class it would log as worthless or losing?
ruling: CLOSED AS PASSED. The node validates the DECISION SYSTEM, not a strategy, and that distinction is enforced on the artifact rather than asserted in prose: every record carries its class's M22 verdict inline, so no logged decision can be read as a claim the opportunity is good. 34 decisions were logged against a live board with a minimum lead of 20,292s (5.6h) to the outcome window, median 26.6h, verified against the ledger on disk. All four refusals were the PROMO-EXAMPLE offers -- coordinator-invented examples with no commence_time -- refused loudly rather than dropped, which is the guard working. Criterion 1: a started game, a game commencing exactly now, and an opportunity with no commence_time are each refused; the quote acted on carries its own capture timestamp and age at decision. Criterion 2: append-only, revisions are new records carrying supersedes, and every on-disk record's own sha256 verifies. Criterion 3: M21 slippage (p90 1.351% at 50 USD, 5.229% at 100) and the measured 49.01 USD median depth applied, with the UNADJUSTED figure retained beside the adjusted one, and book-side limits carried as ABSENT because M21 refused to estimate them. Criterion 4: order_placed and real_money_touched are literal False, mode is SHADOW, there is no venue client or credential read, and S42 IS ENFORCED IN CODE -- a fitted-scoring-model class raises S42Violation and cannot enter the ledger. TESTS.py 32/32 with three tamper tests producing five failures. NOT ESTABLISHED, RECORDED: no outcome has been scored (the games commence 2026-08-22/23, and scoring them is future work needing outcomes this repo does not yet hold); no profitability claim of any kind is made and this ledger may never be cited against M32's -7.2% or M22's verdicts; the run is a single snapshot so nothing about decision arrival rate is established; and a fill 'at median depth' is an assumption applied to a decision, not an observed fill. Seventeen of the 34 decisions sit in a class already measured as negative expectation -- recorded honestly rather than filtered out, because filtering the board would make the ledger a curated exhibit instead of evidence.

WNBA_OddsCapture carries two triggers, confirmed from its task XML and corroborated by the tape: PT15M from 10:00 ET for 5 hours (14:00-19:00 UTC, daytime, 900s gaps) and PT5M from 15:00 ET for 8 hours (19:00-03:00 UTC, the game window, 300s gaps). (1) M03: its own table already showed a five-minute-era p90 of 15.0 min -- that WAS the second tier, and the coordinator read it as noise. The median of 5.0 is a pooled figure over a bimodal distribution; not wrong, but incomplete on a node whose entire subject is cadence. (2) M24: the finding that the 300s freshness cap rejects the board's own 406s-old quote was CORRECTLY OBSERVED BUT WRONGLY EXPLAINED -- the coordinator concluded the decision path was too slow. authority: GRAPH_POLICY s13 E0 exploration; M33; D150; D169; M00 contract
question: M33 said the model-market gap is entirely minutes and needs a 40% error cut. D169 said the cold-start repair helped where the market does not compete. So on the PRICED population, is the remaining minutes error a limit or another defect?
ruling: A DEFECT, AND IT IS CONCENTRATED. On 5,889 priced player-games the arm falls back to a prefix mean for minutes on 519 rows -- 8.8% of the population -- and those rows carry 42.3% of the entire competitive deficit to the market, 95% CI [31.7, 51.9] game-clustered, 2000 draws, seed 20260824. THE MARKET DOES NOT DEGRADE ON THEM: its MAE is flat at 4.86-4.97 across every fallback level while the model's runs 5.11 / 6.02 / 7.24. This is therefore not an intrinsically unpredictable population; the degradation is ours. At fallback level 3 (168 rows) the model under-forecasts minutes by 6.048 and emits an effectively constant value (variance 5e-05 across 168 heterogeneous player-games) -- the SAME degenerate-constant failure mode D150 found, still live in the repaired rev-9 arm. WHY THIS IS NOT A RE-RUN OF D150: that repair landed on largely UNPRICED cold-start rows, which is exactly why D169 measured it moving the verdict by a net one call. These 519 rows ARE priced, so a repair here lands where the market competes. AS A BOUND, NOT A PLAN: if fallback rows reached parity with non-fallback rows, points MAE improves 0.1150 [0.0685, 0.1655] against a current gap of 0.3093 -- 37% of the whole model-vs-market gap. Set against M33's 'needs a 40% minutes-error cut and will not come from another feature sweep', more than a third of the gap sits in under a tenth of the rows, in a code path that emits a prefix mean. A METHOD NOTE WORTH KEEPING: a first pass identified these rows by grouping predictions on repeated values and found 168 rows carrying 22% of the deficit. The arm's own is_fallback/fallback_level flags find 519 carrying 42%. THE HEURISTIC UNDERSTATED THE FINDING BY TWO THIRDS, and the flags were available the whole time. NOT ESTABLISHED: this says nothing about HOW to fix it; the parity counterfactual is a ceiling and these players genuinely have 0-2 prior games (median 1); the market's flat MAE proves the rows are predictable by SOMEONE, not from our feature set -- it may be reading confirmed lineups and late scratches we do not hold; n is 168 at the worst level. NO WAGERING CLAIM: a smaller model-market gap is not an edge, and M32's -7.2% stands untouched.

authority: GRAPH_POLICY s13 E0 exploration; D182; M33
question: D182 quoted a 37% parity ceiling for repairing the minutes fallback rows. What does a realistic, walk-forward repair actually deliver?
ruling: ABOUT 7% OF THE GAP, NOT 37%, AND D182's FRAMING IS CORRECTED IN TWO PLACES. (1) THE TWO FALLBACK LEVELS ARE DIFFERENT PROBLEMS. Level 3 (168 rows) is a genuine degenerate constant: 3 distinct values, sd 0.007. Level 2 (351 rows) is NOT: 339 distinct values, sd 5.50, spanning 4.35 to 39.90 -- the model uses per-row information there and a single constant would be WORSE (a median constant loses 13.2%). So D182's 'analysis 519 rows take a prefix mean' was too broad; only 168 do, and the other 351 need something else entirely. (2) THE REPAIR IS AN ORDER SMALLER THAN THE CEILING. Replacing the constant with a WALK-FORWARD value -- the prior-season priced-population mean, 30.09, knowable before any of these games and available for 127 of 168 rows -- takes minutes MAE on those rows from 7.460 to 5.405 and moves the overall competitive response from -0.3093 to -0.2872: SEVEN PERCENT of the gap. The oracle median of actuals delivers the same 7%, so nothing is lost by staying walk-forward. The 37% was a PARITY ceiling across all 519 rows and a constant cannot reach it, because the points error on those rows has sources a minutes constant does not touch. WHY THE CONSTANT IS WRONG IS NOW DIAGNOSED, and it is a selection effect rather than a modelling failure: 21.51 is a prefix mean over a population including bench players, applied to priced rows that are 74% starters averaging 27.6 minutes against the priced population's 28.9. The constant is not wrong in general; it is wrong for the subpopulation it lands on. STANDING CORRECTION TO HOW I REPORT CEILINGS: D182 labelled 37% a bound in its report but I led with it, and a ceiling quoted without its realistic counterpart reads as a forecast. The repair remains real, cheap and walk-forward -- it is simply worth 7%.

authority: GRAPH_POLICY s13 E0 exploration; D182; D183; M33; M00 contract
question: s02 fixed the level-3 constant for 7%. Level 2 is twice the rows and is not a constant problem. What is it, and what are both repairs worth when the tuning is done honestly?
ruling: LEVEL 2 IS A RATE PROBLEM, NOT A MINUTES PROBLEM, AND THE TWO REPAIRS TOGETHER CLOSE 21.3% OF THE GAP ON HELD-OUT DATA. An oracle decomposition within fallback levels separates them cleanly: level 0 goes -0.196 as-is to +0.408 with oracle minutes, so correcting minutes makes the model BEAT the market there; level 3 goes -2.381 to -0.362, so 85% of its deficit is minutes, consistent with the constant diagnosis; but level 2 goes -1.054 to only -0.592, so oracle minutes recovers UNDER HALF and minutes is not its main problem. Its rate MAE is 0.1945 against level 0's 0.1601 with a bias of +0.0372 points per minute -- about a point of systematic over-prediction across 29 minutes, which is textbook small-sample over-fitting: a player who scored well in one or two prior games gets an inflated rate. TWO REPAIRS, BOTH WALK-FORWARD. Level 3: replace the prefix-mean constant with the prior-season priced-population mean minutes. Level 2: shrink the fitted rate toward the prior-season priced-population mean rate. Every constant comes from strictly earlier seasons and was knowable before the games. THE TUNING IS HONEST, AND s02's WAS NOT. s02 chose its shrinkage weight by maximising the response on the same rows it reported -- in-sample tuning, which is precisely the error the level-2 rows themselves commit. Here w is chosen on 2024-2025 alone (w=0.60) and evaluated on 2026, which never informed the choice. HELD-OUT 2026, 2,005 rows: -0.3108 to -0.2447, 21.3% of the gap closed. Level-3 constant alone -0.2751, level-2 shrinkage alone -0.2805, both -0.2447; the repairs touch disjoint row sets and are close to additive. Held-out improvement EXCEEDS the fit-season improvement, which argues the repairs generalise rather than over-fit. WHAT THIS IS NOT. The model STILL LOSES: -0.2447 remains negative and the market is still better on the priced population. Closing part of a deficit is not an edge and nothing here revisits M32's -7.2%. NEITHER REPAIR IS IMPLEMENTED -- the arm is registered and byte-locked, and changing it is a new revision, not a diagnostic's business. The level-3 constant is available for only 127 of 168 rows and the level-2 prior for 255 of 351; first-season rows have no prior by construction.

authority: M00 final_state_archive_ruling M00-U4; node stop conditions; GRAPH_POLICY s13
question: Level 0 is 91% of priced rows and oracle minutes there makes the model BEAT the market. What drives its minutes error, and can it be fixed?
ruling: GAME SCRIPT DRIVES IT, THE CEILING IS MODEST, AND THE OBVIOUS TEST IS PROHIBITED. Level-0 minutes error correlates 0.2975 with the final margin and the bias gradient is monotonic across margin buckets: the model UNDER-forecasts minutes by 1.177 in games decided by 0-5 and OVER-forecasts by 3.581 in blowouts of 21+. It does not anticipate how competitive a game will be, and starters sit in blowouts. CEILING, MEASURED FROM OUTCOMES AND NOT FROM ANY ODDS ARCHIVE: removing the margin-conditional bias entirely takes level-0 minutes MAE 4.0651 to 3.8249 and the response -0.1957 to -0.1502, about 23% of level-0's deficit. That uses the FINAL MARGIN, is pure oracle, bounds the prize and is not achievable. HALT RAISED RATHER THAN STRETCHING THE ENUMERATION. The natural test -- does the pre-game spread anticipate the margin well enough to fix this -- CANNOT BE RUN. data/drive_masters/master_odds.csv carries odds_spread over the right seasons, but M00's final-state archive ruling enumerates six permitted uses and M00-U4 states the archive is for coarse descriptive context, NEVER A FEATURE, NEVER A BENCHMARK. Using its spread as a minutes feature is outside the enumeration and this lane's stop condition is explicit. The cutoff-valid alternative, data/odds_capture, begins 2026-07-30 -- the day the priced frame ends -- so there is no legal pre-game spread for this window at all. Amending the enumeration is a contract change and is not a coordinator's to make silently. A POINT THAT OUTLIVES THE BLOCK AND SHOULD SURVIVE ANY LATER AMENDMENT: even with permission, closing the gap by feeding the model the market's own spread imports market information. It moves the model TOWARD the market asymptotically, not past it. This route can narrow the deficit; it CANNOT produce edge and must never be sold as a path to one. That distinction matters more than the block, because a future coordinator granted the permission could close the gap and mistake it for progress toward profitability.

authority: user instruction 2026-08-24 responding to a specific request; M33; M38; M35
question: John asked how an absent WNBA starter's minutes actually redistribute before we model it, and instructed: do whatever we need to do in terms of the cutoff question. What does the data say, and what is now authorised?
ruling: THE MECHANISM IS MEASURED, AND THE CUTOFF WORK IS AUTHORISED. On 631 clean team-games where exactly one rotation regular (15+ minute baseline) was absent and 7+ teammates played, that player normally plays 22.6 minutes. Of those minutes the single biggest gainer absorbs 59% (median), the top two absorb 98%, and a median of 6 of 9 teammates who played gain something. So it is NEITHER one designated substitute NOR an even spread: one player takes the bulk, a second takes most of the rest, and a broad group picks up small change. WHO ABSORBS IS PARTLY PREDICTABLE, AND THE CIRCULAR MEASUREMENT MUST NOT BE QUOTED. Scoring 'was it the same player again' over the same events gives 64% mean / 50% median, but that is inflated by construction -- with two events the most common absorber is at minimum 50%. The PREDICTIVE test, forecasting each absence's absorber from PRIOR absences only, scores 133 of 368 = 36% against an 11% chance level, a 3.3x lift. Both are reported in the artifact so the difference is visible; only 36% may be cited. ARCHITECTURAL CONSEQUENCE: a hard depth-chart successor would be wrong about two times in three, so the right shape is a PROBABILISTIC SHARE REALLOCATION -- freed minutes distributed across teammates by a learned propensity with most of the mass on one or two, not handed to a designated heir. This also fits the hard constraint the current model ignores entirely: team minutes are 200 per game, with 95.6% of team-games within one minute of exactly 200, while the present model forecasts every player from her own history alone with no teammate term anywhere in it. THE CUTOFF AUTHORISATION. John instructed 'do whatever we need to do in terms of the cutoff question' in direct response to a request for a specific instruction, which discharges the blanket-yes objection recorded in D181. This is recorded as authorisation to DO THE CUTOFF WORK. It does NOT retroactively reinterpret any existing receipted figure: every published number was computed under the current policy mix and keeps its meaning. The redistribution model cannot run at all without knowing who is out before tip, so the cutoff is now the binding prerequisite for the single largest identified model improvement rather than an abstract contract question.

authority: user instruction 2026-08-24; D186; M35; M38
question: The cutoff work is authorised. What does the current forecast cutoff actually cost, measured in the input the minutes model needs -- knowing who is out?
ruling: IT COSTS ALMOST EVERYTHING. Measured on the injury tape's 144 player-games carrying an Out designation, the share of Out designations ALREADY PUBLISHED at each candidate cutoff is: the current day-before default 8.3%, T-6h 43.8%, T-90m 51.4%, T-30m 74.3%. Median first publication is 1.5 HOURS before tip, p25 0.3h, p75 22.4h -- half of all Out news breaks inside ninety minutes of tip. This is late-breaking news, not a day-ahead list, and the day-before cutoff sees essentially none of it. MOVING TO T-90m IS A 6.2x IMPROVEMENT in the single input a minutes-redistribution model cannot run without. THIS IS A DIFFERENT MEASUREMENT FROM THE EARLIER CUTOFF WORK AND SUPERSEDES IT AS THE DECISION-RELEVANT ONE. M35 asked whether the tape was VISIBLE at a cutoff, which is a property of the tape and of the contract. This asks whether the news had BEEN PUBLISHED yet, which is the property the model consumes. A tape we may legally read is worthless if the news has not broken. IT ALSO EXPLAINS A RESULT THAT HAS SAT UNEXPLAINED SINCE M38: the market's forecast error is FLAT across our thin-history and fallback rows while ours degrades sharply, which M38 could only record as 'the rows are predictable by someone'. The someone is reading roster news that our own cutoff has contractually declined to look at. That is not a modelling deficiency; it is an information deficiency we imposed on ourselves. LIMITS, AND THEY ARE REAL. 144 player-games in a single late-season window, 2026-08-06 to 08-22. Roster news may break differently in April than in August. The ET-to-UTC conversion is a fixed -4 offset, correct for this window and wrong in general. The DIRECTION is not in doubt -- an 8.3% to 51.4% gap cannot be a sampling artifact -- but the exact percentages are provisional. NOTHING RETROACTIVE. No existing receipted figure is reinterpreted; every published number was computed under the current policy mix and keeps its meaning.

authority: GRAPH_POLICY s13 E0 exploration; D186; D187; M33
question: The redistribution mechanism is real and the tip source now lights up who is out. Bolted onto the existing per-player EWMA, what does redistributing an absent regular's minutes actually buy?
ruling: ESSENTIALLY NOTHING -- 0.55% of teammate minutes MAE -- AND THE TEST WAS GENEROUS TO THE IDEA. On 631 single-absence team-games covering 5,700 teammate rows: current model 4.9009 minutes MAE; proportional redistribution of the freed minutes at the best fraction 4.8739 (-0.55%); redistribution CONCENTRATED on the walk-forward predicted absorber 4.8788 (-0.45%). Concentrating is WORSE than spreading, because the absorber is identified only 36% of the time and the 64% of misses cost more than the hits gain. REDISTRIBUTING THE FULL FREED AMOUNT IS 9% WORSE than doing nothing, with bias flipping from -0.64 to +2.07: naive redistribution massively over-allocates. The optimal fraction is about 0.20, meaning only a fifth of an absent regular's minutes flow proportionally to teammates who were already playing -- the rest goes to deep-bench players who would not otherwise appear, or is already absorbed in the teammates' own baselines. THE TEST WAS RIGGED IN THE IDEA'S FAVOUR AND STILL FAILED. Redistribution was applied only among players who ACTUALLY PLAYED, which is post-hoc knowledge no forecaster has at the cutoff. A production version must decide who is activated before it can allocate to them. Even with that unearned advantage the gain is half a percent. WHAT THIS DOES AND DOES NOT KILL. It kills REDISTRIBUTION AS A PATCH on the existing per-player EWMA. It does NOT kill the share architecture: predicting each player's SHARE of the 200 team-minutes for the whole roster and renormalising is a different construction that handles activation endogenously, and nothing here tests it. The mechanism measured in D186 is real -- one teammate absorbs 59%, two absorb 98% -- but a real mechanism is not automatically an exploitable one, and the identification accuracy is the binding constraint rather than the mechanism's existence. NOTHING ABOUT THE CUTOFF WORK IS WASTED: knowing who is out remains a prerequisite for any version, and D187's 8.3%-to-51.4% finding stands.

authority: GRAPH_POLICY s13 E0 exploration; D186; D188
question: John's instinct is that replacement is position/player/team specific and may need research beyond the data, but asked to exhaust what we have first. What is the ceiling on identifying WHO absorbs an absent regular's minutes from box-score data alone?
ruling: THE CEILING IS ABOUT 3.4x CHANCE AND IT IS NOT ENOUGH. Signal inventory over 631 single-absence team-games: the player PROMOTED into the vacated starting slot is the absorber 49.0% of the time against a 14.5% chance level (3.38x, n=414) -- the strongest signal found, but starting lineups are announced roughly 10-30 minutes before tip, AFTER a T-90m cutoff, so it is probably unusable in production. Player-pair history predicts the absorber 36% against 11% (3.3x) and IS available at any cutoff. Position match is far weaker than it first appeared and the distinction matters: the absorber SHARES the absent player's position 42.5% of the time against 30.2% chance (1.41x), but PICKING the best position-matched candidate identifies the absorber only 17.8% of the time, because several teammates share a position and knowing it barely narrows the field. TWO RESULTS WORTH KEEPING. Picking the highest-baseline teammate identifies the absorber 1.0% of the time -- far BELOW the 11% chance level, so it is actively anti-predictive: the absorber is not the best player but the one with ROOM TO GROW, since the top player is already near her minutes ceiling. And a hand-weighted combination of pair, position and baseline scored 8.6%, also below chance; the combination attempt simply failed and is recorded as a failure rather than tuned until it flattered. JOHN'S INSTINCT IS SUPPORTED BY THE EVIDENCE. Box-score data tops out around 3.3x chance on the usable signal, and D188 already showed that at 36% identification a concentrated allocation performs WORSE than a proportional one, because the 64% of misses cost more than the hits gain. Closing this properly does look like it needs team-and-rotation-specific knowledge that box scores do not carry -- beat reporting, coach tendency, depth-chart intent. WHAT IS NOT KILLED: the share architecture across the full roster remains untested, and the promoted-starter signal would be strong IF a lineup source arriving before the cutoff existed. Whether one does is a data-acquisition question, not a modelling one.

authority: GRAPH_POLICY s13 E0 exploration; D186; D187; D188; D189
question: The share architecture was the last untested idea. Does predicting each player's share of the 200 team-minutes beat the current absolute-minutes EWMA?
ruling: ONLY IF YOU KNOW WHO PLAYS -- AND THAT, NOT THE ALLOCATION FORMULA, IS THE BINDING CONSTRAINT. A four-way decomposition over ~28,000 player-games in ~3,040 team-games isolates which piece of knowledge carries the value. Current absolute EWMA 4.7173 minutes MAE. Share model with an ORACLE roster and an ORACLE team total 4.5581 (-3.4%). Share model with an ORACLE ROSTER but the honest 200 constant 4.6330 (-1.8%) -- STILL BETTER THAN CURRENT. Share model with an EXPECTED roster but the oracle team total 4.8451 (+2.7%) -- WORSE. Share model fully honest, expected roster and 200 constant, 4.8999 (+3.9%) -- WORSE. SO THE ROSTER CARRIES ESSENTIALLY ALL THE VALUE AND THE TEAM TOTAL CARRIES ALMOST NONE. Knowing exactly who will play is worth about 1.8% of minutes MAE on its own; knowing the exact team total while guessing the roster LOSES 2.7%. A FIRST PASS OVERSTATED THIS AND THE LEAK IS RECORDED. The share model initially showed -3.4%, but that scaled by each game's ACTUAL team total and normalised across only the players who ACTUALLY PLAYED -- both post-hoc. Closing the two leaks flips the result from -3.4% to +3.9%, an entirely leak-driven finding, and the decomposition above exists because the first number was not trusted. WHY THE HONEST VERSION LOSES: the expected roster (anyone who played in the team's last three games) is larger than the set who actually play, so every player's share is diluted and minutes are under-predicted by 1.12 on average. Over-inclusion, not the formula, is the defect. THIS UNIFIES THE WHOLE THREAD. D188 killed redistribution-as-a-patch; D189 found box-score absorber identification tops out at 3.3x chance; and this shows the allocation formula was never the problem. Every route reduces to the same question -- WHO IS ON THE FLOOR -- which is precisely what D187 measured the cutoff as costing: 8.3% of Out designations visible at the current cutoff against 51.4% at T-90m. The cutoff work is not adjacent to the minutes problem; it IS the minutes problem.

authority: GRAPH_POLICY s13 E0 exploration; D186; D188; D189; D190; M33
question: Build the roster model. Does predicting who is on the floor, then allocating minutes under the 200-minute constraint, beat the current unconstrained per-player forecast?
ruling: BUILT FOUR WAYS. NONE OF THEM WORKS, AND THE REASON IS MECHANICAL. Baseline: the arm's conditional minutes forecast scored on players who actually played, MAE 5.3920, bias -0.1417. (1) Renormalising the arm's own expected minutes to the 200 constraint: 5.6885 vs 5.8816 unnormalised -- better than the unnormalised version but both far worse than simply using the conditional forecast, because multiplying by p_active under-predicts a population selected on having played. (2) Scaling conditional minutes by the team's expected total (200 / sum of p*m): 5.5328, +2.61% WORSE, bias flipping -0.14 to +1.19. (3) Hard predicted roster from p_active at five thresholds, then shares normalised within it: best case 5.5298 at threshold 0.6 with roster size 9.6 and recall 0.938, still +2.56% WORSE; at threshold 0.9 recall collapses to 0.546 and MAE degrades 35%. (4) An independent share-EWMA model, D190, +3.9% worse honestly. WHY, AND THIS IS THE TRANSFERABLE PART: CONSTRAINT ENFORCEMENT AMPLIFIES ROSTER ERROR RATHER THAN TOLERATING IT. Normalising to a fixed total means one wrongly-included player dilutes every teammate and one wrongly-excluded player inflates them all. At recall 0.938 -- a good roster predictor, and the arm's p_active is genuinely decent at AUC 0.8683 and Brier 30.6% better than base rate -- the composition error already costs more than the constraint buys. The team's expected total averages 188.7 against a true 200, but that 11.3-minute shortfall is NOT systematic under-prediction of the players who play; it is largely correct discounting of players who do not, so scaling everyone up over-corrects. THE PRIZE WAS SMALL ANYWAY, AND TWO ORACLES MUST NOT BE CONFLATED. D190's oracle-ROSTER bound is 1.8% of minutes MAE -- knowing exactly who plays while still forecasting their minutes by EWMA. That is a completely different quantity from M33's oracle-MINUTES result of +0.408 response, which assumes PERFECT minutes. Solving the roster perfectly does not deliver perfect minutes and must never be quoted as though it did. WHAT REMAINS: the mechanism measured in D186 is real, the cutoff finding in D187 stands, and knowing who is out is still a prerequisite for anything here -- but on this evidence the roster route does not close the model-market gap, and I am not able to make it do so from the data available.

authority: GRAPH_POLICY s13 E0 exploration; D185; D188; D189; D190; D191
question: D185 blocked the market's spread as a game-script feature. Our OWN team-strength differential, derived from box scores, is not blocked. Does it recover the game-script effect?
ruling: NO. IT PREDICTS THE WRONG HALF OF THE PROBLEM. A trailing point-differential strength estimate, prior games only, correlates 0.4534 with the SIGNED final margin over 1,355 games -- it knows who wins and roughly by how much. But the minutes effect runs on BLOWOUT-NESS, and the same estimate correlates only 0.1665 with |margin|. Predicted-lopsided games average 13.3 actual |margin| against 10.3 for predicted-close: a real gradient across the full range of only three points. Walk-forward, fitting the minutes-bias-versus-expected-blowout slope on strictly earlier seasons and applying it to the held-out season, minutes MAE goes 4.6825 to 4.7389 -- 1.20% WORSE. The correction is not merely useless; it is harmful, because a weak predictor of blowout-ness applied as a bias correction adds more noise than it removes. WHY THIS MATTERS BEYOND THE RESULT: D185 recorded the game-script route as contract-blocked and left the impression that permission was the binding constraint. It is not. The unblocked substitute was tried and fails on its own merits, so the block is no longer load-bearing for this route and should not be cited as though the answer is waiting behind it. THIS IS THE FIFTH CONSECUTIVE NEGATIVE ON THE MINUTES CHANNEL: redistribution as a patch (D188), box-score absorber identification (D189), the share architecture (D190), the roster model in four constructions (D191), and now game script from our own strength. The minutes channel is not improvable from the data this programme holds, and further attempts should carry a specific new information source rather than a new arrangement of the same features.

authority: GRAPH_POLICY s13 E0 exploration; D187; D188; D189; D190; D191; D192; M38
question: D192 said further minutes attempts should carry a NEW information source rather than a rearrangement. Rest days are exactly that -- absent from the minutes leg entirely. Does schedule density predict minutes error?
ruling: A CLEAN NULL, AND IT CLOSES THE CHANNEL. Over 27,455 player-games with team rest known, the correlation between days of rest and minutes error is -0.0048. Bias by rest bucket: back-to-back -0.182 (n=831), two days -0.220, three days -0.094, four or more -0.148 -- a spread of 0.13 minutes across the entire range. Actual mean minutes are 21.4, 21.3, 21.3, 21.4 respectively: INDISTINGUISHABLE. Back-to-backs do not measurably reduce WNBA minutes in this data, which is a hypothesis most people would assume true without checking, and it is worth recording as a null precisely because of that. THE MINUTES CHANNEL IS NOW CLOSED FROM DATA THIS PROGRAMME HOLDS. Six independent attempts, all negative: redistribution as a patch (D188, 0.5% and worse when concentrated), box-score absorber identification (D189, ceiling 3.3x chance and insufficient), the share architecture (D190, 3.9% worse honestly), the roster model in four constructions (D191, all worse, with constraint enforcement amplifying roster error rather than tolerating it), game script from our own strength differential (D192, 1.20% worse walk-forward), and schedule density (here, null). WHAT WOULD CHANGE THIS IS DATA, NOT METHOD. The market's forecast error is FLAT across the row classes where ours degrades sharply (M38), so the information exists and somebody holds it; D187 measured that our own cutoff sees 8.3% of Out designations against 51.4% at T-90m; and D189 found the strongest identification signal, the promoted starter at 3.38x chance, arrives with the starting lineup roughly 10-30 minutes before tip. Every one of those points at ROSTER AND ROLE NEWS we do not currently capture -- confirmed lineups, beat reporting, depth-chart intent -- rather than at another arrangement of box-score features. RECOMMENDATION, NOT A DECISION: stop testing rearrangements of held data on this channel. The next honest step is acquiring a pre-tip lineup or roster-intent source, which is a data-acquisition question for the user, not a modelling one.

authority: GRAPH_POLICY s13 E0 exploration; D189; D193
question: John asked for dynamic minutes driven by deep knowledge of who takes a benched starter's minutes. The programme holds 996 play-by-play files never used for this. Do in-game substitution patterns identify the absorber?
ruling: NO, AND THE REASON IS A GENUINELY NON-OBVIOUS FACT ABOUT ROTATIONS. 39,421 substitution events were extracted from 996 play-by-play files (EVENTMSGTYPE 8; PLAYER1 out, PLAYER2 in, verified against the event text 'SUB: Holmes FOR Shook') and written to data/derived/substitutions.parquet -- a source this programme had never touched for this question. Walk-forward, predicting a whole-game absence's absorber as the teammate who most often subbed IN for her in PRIOR games scores 80 of 581 = 13.8% against an 11.2% chance level. A 1.23x lift, and FAR WORSE than the 3.3x that plain box-score pair history achieves. THE DIAGNOSIS IS THE VALUABLE PART. The absorber does appear somewhere in the absent player's substitution history 75.7% of the time, so the data is connected and the join is sound. But her MEDIAN RANK among that player's substitutes is FOURTH: top-1 14.3%, top-2 29.1%, top-3 37.2%. So WHO SPELLS YOU FOR A SHIFT IS NOT WHO REPLACES YOU FOR A GAME. A mid-game substitution is whoever is next in the rotation at that moment; a whole-game absence makes the coach RESTRUCTURE, typically promoting a different starter-quality player while the direct backup continues playing her own minutes regardless. This refutes a natural and widely-held assumption -- it was the coordinator's expectation and the user's -- and it is recorded because the assumption is the kind that would otherwise be built on. WHAT REMAINS UNTRIED ON THIS SOURCE: substitution PAIRS were tested, but not lineup COMPLEMENTARITY -- which players' court time is negatively correlated with hers across stints. That requires reconstructing five-player stints from the play-by-play rather than reading sub events, is a materially larger build, and is the last construction this data supports. SEVENTH CONSECUTIVE NEGATIVE on the minutes channel; D193's recommendation stands unless complementarity changes it.

authority: GRAPH_POLICY s13 E0 exploration; D188; D189; D193; D194
question: D194 left lineup complementarity as the last construction the play-by-play supports. Does 'who plays when she does not' identify the absorber, and does combining signals help?
ruling: IT IS THE SECOND-BEST SIGNAL AND STILL NOT ENOUGH; THE INVENTORY IS NOW COMPLETE. FIRST, A BUILD THAT FAILED AND WAS NOT PATCHED AROUND: full five-player stint reconstruction from play-by-play was attempted and reconstructed only 2 of 996 games. The cause is real and not a coding slip -- SUBSTITUTIONS AT PERIOD BOUNDARIES ARE NOT RECORDED AS SUB EVENTS. Player 1630446 is flagged a starter in the box score yet her first play-by-play appearance is ENTERING in period 2, so any walk assuming every lineup change emits an event desynchronises. The validation caught it and DISCARDED 994 games rather than emitting partially-correct stints, which is the correct behaviour: a drifted lineup would look usable and be wrong. Proper reconstruction needs period-start lineups inferred separately and was not attempted. COMPLEMENTARITY WAS THEN MEASURED WITHOUT STINTS, from game-level minutes correlation -- the teammate whose minutes correlate most NEGATIVELY with hers over prior games in the same team-season. 143 of 578 = 24.7% against 11.1% chance, a 2.23x lift. Better than substitution pairs (1.23x) and position (1.4x), still well below plain pair history (3.24x). COMBINING BUYS COVERAGE, NOT ACCURACY. A hierarchical predictor -- pair history where a prior absence exists, complementarity otherwise -- scores 30.7% over 587 events at 2.75x, against pair history's 36.1% over 368 at 3.24x. It fires on 60% more events at lower accuracy. No free lunch, and no combination beats pair history where pair history applies. THE INVENTORY IS COMPLETE AND THE CEILING IS 3.3x. Every absorber-identification signal the held data supports has now been measured: pair history 3.24x, complementarity 2.23x, position 1.4x, in-game substitution pairs 1.23x, highest-baseline teammate 0.09x (anti-predictive). D188 already established that at 36% identification a concentrated allocation performs WORSE than a proportional one. So the ceiling is known, it is insufficient, and no further arrangement of these features will change it. EIGHTH CONSECUTIVE NEGATIVE. D193's recommendation now stands unqualified: the next honest step on this channel is a pre-tip lineup or roster-intent source, which is a data-acquisition question.

authority: user instruction 2026-08-24 relaxing the research cutoff; D188; D189; M21; M17
question: John ruled that the T-90m cutoff need not be enforced -- any information held before tip-off is usable, because the bet can be placed before tip. What does that unlock?
ruling: IT UNLOCKS THE SIGNAL THAT WAS ALREADY THE STRONGEST, AND PRODUCES THE FIRST POSITIVE RESULT ON THIS CHANNEL AFTER EIGHT NEGATIVES. D189 measured the promoted starter -- the player who takes a vacated starting slot -- as identifying the absorber 49.0% of the time against 14.5% chance (3.38x), and DISMISSED it because starting lineups are announced 10-30 minutes before tip, after the T-90m cutoff. Under the new ruling that dismissal no longer applies. D188 had established that at 36% identification a concentrated allocation is WORSE than a proportional one. At 49% it is BETTER, and that is the whole difference. WALK-FORWARD VALIDATED, PARAMETERS CHOSEN ON EARLIER SEASONS ONLY: 2022 -2.15%, 2023 -1.52%, 2024 -4.06%, 2025 -1.34%, 2026 -1.74%. Pooled held-out minutes MAE 4.8450 to 4.7431, -2.10%. It improves in EVERY one of five seasons, and the chosen parameters converge on roughly 30% of the freed minutes with 75% of that concentrated on the promoted starter, rather than jumping around -- stability, not noise-chasing. An in-sample read of the same grid gave -2.49%; the walk-forward figure of -2.10% is the one to quote. TWO CONDITIONS THIS RESULT DEPENDS ON, AND NEITHER IS YET MET. FIRST, THE INPUT IS NOT WIRED: the test uses the box-score starter flag as a PROXY for the announced lineup. In production this needs a real pre-tip lineup source, which the programme does not currently capture. The signal is demonstrated; the feed does not exist. SECOND, AND MORE IMPORTANT: THE MARKET SEES THE LINEUP TOO. Moving our information set to T-30m means every model-versus-market comparison must use CONTEMPORANEOUS T-30m market prices. Scoring a lineup-aware model against a T-90m market price would manufacture an edge out of a timing mismatch, and would be the single easiest way to fool this programme into believing it had found one. -2.10% is a MINUTES improvement and is NOT a demonstrated edge. ALSO NOT SETTLED: only 484 of 631 absence events have a promoted starter; point-in-time integrity still requires PROVING we held the lineup before tip rather than assuming it, which is what the existing fail-closed machinery is for; and liquidity and limits near tip are M21/M17 territory and unmeasured at that horizon.

authority: user instruction 2026-08-24 relaxing the research cutoff; D188; D189; D196
question: D196's result needs an announced lineup we do not capture. Can promotion history substitute for the feed, and if not, exactly what is the feed worth?
ruling: HISTORY PREDICTS THE LINEUP WELL AND THE ABSORBER BADLY, SO THE FEED CANNOT BE SUBSTITUTED -- AND IT IS WORTH 1.49 PERCENTAGE POINTS. NO LINEUP FEED EXISTS IN ANYTHING CAPTURED, verified rather than assumed: the injury tape carries STATUS only (Available/Probable/Questionable/Doubtful/Out), and of 12,899 news items just 3 mention a starting lineup, all of them DFS previews rather than announcements. PROMOTION HISTORY -- who has previously started in this player's place -- predicts the ACTUAL promoted starter at 191/247 = 77.3% walk-forward, which is genuinely good. But it predicts the ABSORBER at only 75/247 = 30.4% (2.74x chance), BELOW the 36% that D188 already showed was insufficient for concentrated allocation, and far below the 49.0% obtained when the lineup is KNOWN. The chain degrades because a promotion prediction that misses takes the allocation with it. THE DECISIVE COMPARISON, both walk-forward with parameters chosen on earlier seasons only: known announced lineup improves held-out minutes MAE from 4.8450 to 4.7431 (-2.10%); predicted promotion improves it only to 4.8155 (-0.61%). PREDICTING THE LINEUP CAPTURES 29% OF WHAT KNOWING IT DELIVERS. The feed is worth 1.49 percentage points of minutes MAE, a 3.4x difference, and -0.61% without it is barely distinguishable from the -0.55% that plain proportional redistribution already achieved. THIS IS AN ACQUISITION CASE, NOT A MODELLING ONE, AND IT IS NOW PRICED. A pre-tip lineup source is the difference between a marginal improvement and a meaningful one on the single channel that carries the model-market gap. WHAT IT STILL DOES NOT BUY: -2.10% is a MINUTES improvement, not an edge. Any model-versus-market claim built on lineup-time information MUST be scored against contemporaneous lineup-time market prices, because the market reads the same announcement; comparing a T-30m model to a T-90m price would manufacture an edge from a timing mismatch. That condition from D196 is unchanged and unmet.

authority: M00 stop condition on scraping/licensing risk; D196; D197; RotoWire and SportsDataIO published statements; empirical test of boxscoresummaryv2
question: Find a free lineup feed to scrape. What is actually available, and does it deliver the input D196/D197 priced?
ruling: THE PRODUCT DOES NOT EXIST, AND D197's ACQUISITION CASE IS CORRECTED DOWNWARD ACCORDINGLY. THE LEAGUE ITSELF IS THE CONSTRAINT: the WNBA DOES NOT REQUIRE STARTING LINEUPS TO BE SUBMITTED BEFORE TIPOFF. RotoWire states this directly as the reason it is 'sometimes limited to waiting until a game tips off to accurately pass on who is starting', and SportsDataIO's own workflow guide says WNBA lineups are not confirmed pre-game and must be derived from the box score once the game is in progress. This is structural to WNBA coverage, not a gap in our vendors. WHAT IS ACTUALLY AVAILABLE IS A PROJECTION, NOT A CONFIRMATION. RotoWire publishes an EXPECTED lineup set 24-30 hours before tip and adjusted through gameday, labelled 'Expected' for every game, with confirmation only 'when an official WNBA source provides that information'. THE OFFICIAL SOURCE WE ALREADY CALL DOES NOT CARRY IT EITHER, tested rather than assumed: boxscoresummaryv2 on scheduled game 1022600282 (8:00pm ET tonight, status 1) returns game metadata, series and team frames but NO player rows and no starters. stats.nba.com publishes starters only once the box score exists. THE CORRECTION TO D197. Its -2.10% used the box-score starter flag, which is a CONFIRMED lineup and is therefore NOT OBTAINABLE PRE-TIP FOR THE WNBA. The attainable figure is the PROJECTED one, and our own promotion history already projects the starter at 77.3% for -0.61%. So the 1.49-percentage-point acquisition case largely evaporates: what was priced is not purchasable at any price, free or paid, scraped or licensed. THE NARROW QUESTION THAT REMAINS is whether a third party's expected lineup beats our own 77.3% projection by enough to matter, propagated through a chain that already degrades from 77.3% promotion accuracy to 30.4% absorber accuracy. That is a much smaller prize than 1.49 points and would need their HISTORICAL expectations, which we do not hold and which are not published as an archive. SCRAPING REMAINS USER_REQUIRED REGARDLESS: M00's stop condition makes accepting scraping or licensing risk a user gate, and nothing here resolves it. No source was scraped; two public pages were read and one API we already call was tested.

authority: M00 evidence ladder; D105/D140 operational discipline; observed defects 2026-08-24
question: The lineup parser shipped and ran successfully twice while silently discarding rows, and WNBA_DailyForecast_PM died leaving nothing to read. What is the shared failure, and what is the standing rule?
ruling: BOTH ARE THE SAME DEFECT: a component that FAILS WHILE REPORTING SUCCESS. The parser exited 0 on 19 rows when 23 existed, and both dropped classes were injury-flagged players -- 'is-pct-play-50 has-injury-status' and a lineup__pos div carrying a style attribute -- i.e. it discarded precisely the rows that carry new information, which is the worst possible bias and the hardest to notice. WNBA_DailyForecast_PM aborted on 2026-08-23 and the wrapper discarded its output, so a crashed model and a sleeping machine were indistinguishable; re-running today succeeded, which means the cause was diagnosed by LUCK, not evidence. FOUR THINGS ADOPTED. (1) A parser must compare what it parsed against what was listed and say so when they differ -- the count guard is what surfaced the second bug after the first was fixed. (2) RAW SOURCES ARE RETAINED, which is what made both fixes recoverable: --reparse rebuilt the whole table and the first capture went from 19 rows to 23. Rebuilding a derived view from retained sources is NOT rewriting history; it is what keeps a parser fix from leaving a permanent hole. (3) An unattended job TEES ITS OWN OUTPUT, in the script rather than the task wrapper, because the wrapper is regenerated from wnba_task_actions_backup.json and would lose the edit. This matters most for daily_forecast.py, which writes the official regime-D chain under --live: a prospective record with unexplained holes is worth far less than one whose gaps have known causes. (4) A widened schema must REFUSE to append under a header it does not match -- adding columns beneath the old 11-column header produced a table pandas could not read at all. ALSO CORRECTED: the watchdog reported the newly registered task as failing, because 267011 is SCHED_S_TASK_HAS_NOT_RUN; treating it as a failure means every task is born broken. It caught this on its first run, against my own task.

authority: M00 evidence ladder; M40 s01 walk-forward reconstruction; supersedes the quantitative claims of D198
question: D198 priced a third-party lineup feed on the claim that our own promotion projection is 75.8% with same-season pair history (58% of cases) and 18.5% without (42%). Those numbers were never backed by a script. Do they reproduce?
ruling: NO. M40 s01 rebuilds them from master_player and gets a materially different and much flatter picture over 369 clean single-absence promotions: pair history is available on 23.3% of events, NOT 58%; it scores 40.7%, NOT 75.8%; and the first-time half scores 39.9%, NOT 18.5%, against a 20.3% chance level. Our promotion projection is roughly 40% ACROSS THE BOARD -- a real 2x signal, but a flat one. THE VENDOR CASE FALLS WITH IT. D198 argued a feed was worth buying for the first-time half specifically, because we were supposedly near-blind there. We are not: first-time absences are called marginally BETTER than repeat ones. A vendor must beat ~40% overall rather than rescue an 18.5% hole that does not exist. This does not say a feed is worthless -- the RotoWire capture registered in D199 should still accumulate, and OUT/GTD designations remain valuable in their own right under M39 s02 -- but the specific pricing argument in D198 is withdrawn. SECOND FINDING: pair history is not demonstrably worth its machinery. Against the dumbest available rule -- pick the bench player with the most trailing minutes -- it leads by +7.0pp on its own ground with a 95% PAIRED bootstrap of [-7.0, +19.8] on n=86. The interval spans zero. THIRD FINDING, NEGATIVE AND KEPT: the position filter hurts. The promoted player takes the vacated slot 74.0% of the time, but a candidate pool restricted by prior starts contains the true answer only 64.5% of the time, because the promoted player is very often someone who has never started before. A predictor cannot beat its own pool coverage. The first version of that predictor scored BELOW its own chance level, which was the tell; chance is now defined as the accuracy a random pick inside the pool would actually score -- zero when the pool lacks the answer -- so shrinking a pool past the truth is no longer rewarded. Even repaired it loses, 38.2% vs 39.9%. team_freq (12.0%) and cross_season (2.6%) are dead ends. NOTHING IS BOUND. Limits: n=86 on the repeat half, season-to-season swing of 29.4% to 63.6%, absence inferred from box scores rather than designations, and the 111 dropped multi-absence games are plausibly the harder and more valuable cases.

authority: user standing directive 2026-08-24 to run 24/7 unsupervised; M00 operational discipline; observed outage 2026-08-24
question: On 2026-08-24 the whole capture fleet stopped for 4.5 hours through the evening game window and nothing reported it. Why, and what makes that class of failure visible in future?
ruling: TWO INDEPENDENT FAULTS, the second of which hid the first. (1) BATTERY GATE: 14 of 19 WNBA tasks carried DisallowStartIfOnBatteries=true, the default from New-ScheduledTaskSettingsSet rather than a deliberate choice. The laptop went to battery around 16:42 ET and every capture stopped -- odds, injury-live, market ladder, props, news -- and stayed stopped through the 19:00-03:00 UTC window, which is the 5-minute high-cadence tier and the most valuable capture period of the day. WNBA_DailyForecast_PM also never fired at 18:45, so the official regime-D prospective chain missed a second consecutive night; yesterday's ERROR_PROCESS_ABORTED and tonight's silent skip are both power-related, and the earlier attribution of yesterday's failure to bad luck was diagnosed by luck rather than evidence. The two ungated tasks ran normally throughout, which made the diagnosis unambiguous. All 19 are now ungated, with every definition backed up to logs/task_xml_backup_20260824 first, so it reverts in one pass. The cost is battery drain while unplugged, accepted against the user's standing requirement that this run 24/7 unsupervised -- and this is a settings change on the user's own machine that they may reverse. (2) THE WATCHDOG HAD NO WATCHDOG: WNBA_CaptureHealth's trigger carried Duration=PT13H with StopAtDurationEnd=true, so it repeated hourly for ONE DAY (2026-08-23) and then stopped permanently, reporting state=Ready, rc absent, no next run time. WNBA_OpportunityBoard had the identical bug and had been dead since 2026-08-19. Both now repeat indefinitely. THE STANDING RULE: a task that will never run again is indistinguishable from a healthy one -- Ready, no failure code, nothing amiss -- so capture_health now flags ANY task with no next run time, and that check sits BEFORE the self-exclusion. The self-exclusion exists solely so the watchdog's by-design non-zero exit does not make it cry wolf forever; extending it to the next-run check would blind the watchdog to exactly the failure it just suffered. Verified against a synthetic task table: it flags WNBA_CaptureHealth itself. Note also that tape freshness could not have caught this -- a stale tape looks identical whether the scraper broke or the machine was unplugged. Freshness asks whether data is arriving; the next-run check asks whether anything is still trying.

authority: D199 point-in-time capture; D201; M39 s02; direct observation 2026-08-24
question: The first night of live lineup capture recorded a full revision sequence. What does it establish about how a third-party projection may be evaluated or used?
ruling: THAT A VENDOR PROJECTION MUST BE READ AT A STATED TIME, AND THAT ITS ACCURACY IS A FUNCTION OF THAT TIME. Observed 2026-08-24 for LAS (tip 22:00 ET): at T-4h53m Rae Burrell was listed as a STARTER carrying a GTD flag; at T-57m she was OUT and TONIE MORGAN was projected to replace her; at T-42m the projected replacement CHANGED to MONIQUE AKOA MAKANI; at T-27m it was unchanged. The provider revised its own promotion pick within 15 minutes, so the feed is not a stable oracle -- reading it at T-57m and at T-42m yields DIFFERENT answers, and at most one of them can be right. THREE CONSEQUENCES. (1) Any evaluation of this feed must fix a read time and score that read, because a single end-of-day scrape would have recorded only the final answer and made the feed look perfectly accurate. That is hindsight presented as foresight -- the exact failure the cutoff machinery exists to prevent -- and it would have been invisible without point-in-time capture. This retrospectively justifies the append-only design in D199 over a simpler daily snapshot. (2) Any comparison against our own projection must give BOTH sides the same information cutoff. M40 predicts from prior games only and is therefore available arbitrarily early; the vendor at T-27m is a strictly later read and would win on timing alone if scored carelessly. (3) It sharpens D201: the question is not whether a vendor beats our ~40% but whether it does so AT A TIME WE COULD STILL ACT ON, against contemporaneous market prices. A pick that stabilises at T-27m is worth less than one correct at T-90m, and may be worth nothing if the market has already moved. ALSO NOTED, CONSISTENT WITH M39 s02: Burrell went GTD to OUT inside the final hour, which is the late-breaking pattern that measurement predicted. NOTHING IS BOUND; this is one team on one night and is an observation, not a rate.

authority: direct point-in-time observation 2026-08-24 (ATL@LAS, T-26.9m); D196; D198; D199; D203; user instruction relaxing the research cutoff 2026-08-24
