authority: M00 evidence ladder; M38 s03 (D184) re-derived; arm file-boundary declaration; M41 s01 select-then-confirm
question: M38 s03 (D184) is recorded as the programme's best model-side lead, closing 21.3% of the model's deficit to the market. Before building an arm revision on it, is it implementable inside the arm's contract?
ruling: NO, NOT AS MEASURED. The 21.3% REPRODUCES EXACTLY -- the arithmetic is sound -- but both of s03's constants are means over M33's PRICED FRAME: prior['rate_actual'].mean() and prior['min_actual'].mean() over rows that carried a market price. The arm cannot use that, for two independent reasons. FIRST, it is outside the arm's declared file boundary, which is the contract and the masters read-only; market data is not in it. SECOND, the priced population is selected on the very quantity being predicted, because bookmakers price starters and rotation regulars: prior-season mean minutes is 29.63-30.56 over priced rows against 21.41-21.45 over all rows that played, AN 8-9 MINUTE GAP. Using the priced constant would also mean predicting roughly 30 minutes for deep-bench players on every unpriced row, and the arm emits predictions for all candidates while only a minority are ever priced -- the repair is scored only where it flatters itself. SUBSTITUTING AN ARM-LEGAL GLOBAL CONSTANT LEAVES 6.2%, NOT 21.3%. THE LEAD SURVIVES IN A BETTER FORM. Level 3 does not mean no history; it means no appearance THIS SEASON. 156 of 168 level-3 rows (93%) belong to a player with prior-SEASON minutes of her own. Using HER OWN prior-season mean, falling back to the global constant only where she has none, closes 19.7% on held-out 2026 (-0.3108 -> -0.2495) using nothing but the masters. That is strictly better than what M38 proposed AND it is legal, so the recommended revision changes: implement per-player prior-season minutes, not a population constant. A LOOK IS DECLARED. The own-history variant was written AFTER seeing the global variant score 6.2% on the holdout, which is a second look at 2026. The variants were therefore re-selected on seasons < 2026 alone -- current -0.3084, global -0.2719, own -0.2351 -- and own-history wins outright, so the choice does not depend on the holdout. The ordering is recorded rather than asserted later. LIMITS: w=0.60 stays frozen from s03 and was NOT re-tuned, since re-tuning it beside a changed level-3 rule would select two things on one holdout; held-out n=2005 priced rows and level 3 is 168 rows; the level-2 repair still uses a global prior-season RATE and whether a per-player rate helps there was not tested. NOTHING IS IMPLEMENTED. THE MODEL STILL LOSES: -0.2495 is negative, the market remains better on the priced population, closing part of a deficit is not an edge, and nothing here revisits M32's -7.2%.

authority: M41 s01 (D206); M38 s03 frozen weight; select-then-confirm on seasons < 2026; M00 evidence ladder
question: s01 showed per-player prior-season MINUTES fix level 3 far better than any population constant. Does per-player prior-season RATE do the same for level 2, the other half of M38's repair?
ruling: YES, AND THE FULLY ARM-LEGAL REPAIR NOW BEATS THE NON-LEGAL ONE IT REPLACED. Shrinking the level-2 rate toward HER OWN prior-season rate rather than a global prior-season rate closes 28.3% of the model's deficit on held-out 2026 (-0.3108 -> -0.2230), against 19.7% for the global target. Selection was run on seasons < 2026 alone and picks own-history there too (-0.2221 against -0.2351), so the choice does not depend on the holdout; 95% of level-2 rows have a prior-season rate of their own. THE COMBINED ARM-LEGAL REPAIR -- per-player prior-season MINUTES at level 3, per-player prior-season RATE at level 2 -- THEREFORE CLOSES 28.3%, MORE THAN M38's LEAKY 21.3% (D206), while reading nothing but the masters. The rate is computed as prior points over prior minutes, a ratio of sums rather than a mean of per-game ratios, so a two-minute appearance does not weigh as much as a thirty-five-minute one. w=0.60 REMAINS FROZEN from M38 s03 and was not re-tuned; re-tuning the weight beside a changed shrinkage TARGET would select two things against one holdout. THE READING, WHICH IS NOT WHAT WAS EXPECTED: a level-2 row already carries some current-season evidence, so the shrinkage target could have mattered LESS here than at level 3. It matters MORE. One or two games of current-season EWMA is a worse estimate of a player's scoring rate than her whole previous season -- which is what cbs_v7 meant by calling it 'a fallback wearing a model's clothes', now measured. A METHOD DEFECT WAS FOUND AND FIXED IN THIS FILE: the explanation for why level 2 would NOT behave like level 3 was pre-written and printed unconditionally, so it argued the target 'matters less' while the numbers showed it mattering more. A rationalisation that fires whatever the result is worthless; it is now confined to the branch it describes. NOTHING IS IMPLEMENTED and THE MODEL STILL LOSES: -0.2230 is negative, the market remains better on the priced population, and closing part of a deficit is not an edge.
